reviews.author: Bob Davies
reviews.text: The next patients' group meeting is on the 6th of May at 5pm. We established that patients can arrive a little early (say 10 minutes) to discuss individual problems/experience, so the PPG can focus clearly on shared problems. Whether you can attend or not, please write your review, good or bad, and I will continue to bring them to the new team. From the PPG meeting on Feb 4th... The practice is fully staffed for doctors (now at 6, and 6 admin) but doesn't have a practice manager as they're having trouble recruiting because they will also manage the Oldham practice. I have been assured they're wiring up a better fallback after 2 missed calls (most likely you will receive a text that asks you to ring the practice, but I have asked that a bookable slot picker be added too). The website is now 24hr accessible for admin/repeats, but still cannot be used out of office hours to request an appointment. The doctor has concerns about people using it for 'urgent' requests in the middle of the night (when no doctor is available to receive it), I've tried to make a case for it, but if out of hours appointment-requests is a blocker for you, please come to meetings and help me argue the case. I have also reraised when tests come back all green, but you're still sick, the practice currently close your diagnosis process until you re-engage (which you may not be told you need to do), which I intend to reraise in future. --- From the PPG meeting on November 26th... 2 new doctors are on board, and new staff are coming soon. Complaints about reception seem to be improving, less reliance on agency staff. The website will be switched to 24hr accessible. New Bank is on Bookable, which is much easier to use and is currently accessible outside of office hours (unlike PATCHS), but doesn't work for existing registered patients, and only has a limited number of slots and is only for booking an appointment. --- From the PPG meeting on 10th of September. The practice is moving to a new digital system on 1st of October, which 'should' solve some of the current technical issues with arranging appointments. Management say there will be some onboarding help and open/group sessions for anybody who would like to attend, and dates/times of those will be on a notice-board in the reception (or from Lynne, the operations manager) once those dates are arranged (probably a couple of evenings/saturdays depending on demand). We have also been assurred the quality of help from reception has been better in the last month and will continue to improve. There is still no new practice manager. They are recruiting for one in a difficult market, but they are adding new administrators (from October 6th, if I understood correctly) and _should_ soon be adding extra doctors too, with a less clear timescale (presumably notice-period related). The patient load on doctors is within the normal NHS range, so do not put off making an appointment just because you think they're busy, they have capacity and are adding more, and most of the problems seem to be steadily improving. --- After leaving a previous 1 star review with many negative points and being frustrated with being unable to arrange an appointment, I attended the newly set-up Patient Participation Group meeting (as a new management company took over in April) on 6th August. The discussion between the team and a few patients was constructive and the new management team seem to have an understanding of the problems after we explained in some detail. I also brought these reviews to their attention, and provided a breakdown of reviews to their management in the meeting. If you're here because you've had a negative experience, either recently or before the take-over, we've been assured they're working on it and should be moving to a new system, as well as dealing with the problems caused by specific staff. Please contact management with feedback and come to the patient meeting if you have the time, be heard, the new team are (it seems) finally listening, and they actually have a mandate to fix problems atm.

reviews.text: This practice is one of the worst practices going. The receptionist told me the doctor has received my form and will definitely call me back that same day. I waited and waited, I was so ill I fell asleep and when I woke up I realised they’re closed, I double checked my call logs and I didn’t receive a single call. This has happened to me before where I’ve been ignored by them which is why I called up this time to make sure they’ll definitely call me back. The receptionist falsely reassured me that the doctor would “definitely” call me back that same day. I felt I had an infection and needed antibiotics but they didn’t even bother. I needed an emergency appointment. I waited another day thinking they might’ve been busy but still no call back, I ended up getting better on my own without any support from the gp. I had to call in sick to work as I didn’t have any medication to make me better any sooner. I’ve been feeling ill again for the past week and I’ve not even bothered filling a form in or calling up to book an appointment because of how bad the service is and as I know I’ll just be neglected yet again. This isn’t how one should feel when in need of support. This practice really needs to fix up and get rid of all the slackers.

reviews.text: I'm extremely disappointed with the recent changes at this GP surgery. I had a blood test scheduled but was given a date I couldn’t attend. When I managed to make time, the appointment was cancelled due to "unforeseen circumstances." The new system for ordering medication is also a step backward. It was previously simple to order through the pharmacy app, but now it's linked to the NHS app, which requires identity verification. Despite submitting my details, I'm told it will take several days for confirmation—followed by additional delays for dispensing and delivery. This puts me at risk of running out of essential medication, which is unacceptable. This level of service is deeply concerning. I will be looking to move to a more reliable GP surgery.

reviews.author: Javad Moazami
reviews.rating_label: 1/5 - Extremely DisappointingService Unfortunately, my experience at this clinic was very unpleasant. The behavior of the reception team was seriously unprofessional and disrespectful. On several occasions, they were either absent or busy with other tasks, leaving me waiting for long periods without any guidance. I was never informed that I needed to use the automated check-in system, and even if I had been informed, I would have required assistance. When I encountered disrespectful and insulting behavior, none of the reception staff paid attention to the issue, which caused significant distress and psychological pressure. It seems that the clinic manager is not paying attention to these problems and is not hearing the voices of patients. After sharing this review, I was surprised (and somewhat saddened) to find that several others had similar experiences at this clinic. Given how often such stories seem to come up, it might be worth taking a closer look—not just for me, but for others who may be facing similar situations. In fact, what I’m about to describe is only one of several upsetting experiences I’ve had at this clinic—and sadly, not the last. I am not sure whether this was racially motivated, but the way I was treated was deeply inhumane. I begged them to inform my doctor—who had been regularly renewing my weekly prescription for over a year—that I had run out of critical medication. They completely ignored me and, instead of offering help, shouted at me to leave the clinic. At that very moment, I briefly saw my doctor through a door behind one of the senior staff members—she appeared to say something to someone at a desk and then turned back and disappeared. Still, the staff insisted she wasn’t there. When I told one of the senior team members—who seemed to be in charge or at least more experienced than the others—what I had seen, she and her colleagues pointed at me, laughed at my desperation, and mocked me while I stood there in distress. After being kicked out of the clinic, I walked away with tears in my eyes, feeling utterly humiliated, unwanted, and hopeless. I was in a mental health crisis, and the lack of compassion pushed me to a point where I genuinely started thinking about ending my life. The pain of that moment hasn’t left me—it replays in my mind every single day. The medication that helped me cope was gone, and so was my sense of dignity. And this wasn’t the only time I was treated poorly. I had endured other incidents of disrespect and mistreatment before, but I didn’t know who to turn to or how to raise my concerns. So I kept silent. Eventually, I found the courage to tell my doctor honestly and emotionally what had been happening—only to be removed from the GP a few days later. No one should ever be made to feel that way in a place that is supposed to provide care.

I had Alex hang up the phone on me, ignore phone calls from my number leaving me 1st in the que whenever I called from my number but when I hang up and call straight back with another number she'd answer, a few days went past and I tried calling again to ask for the manager Sharon, and my call was in the que when I was number 1 in the que and no answer, I thought let me call with another phone and join the que, as soon as I did she answered my first call cos now she had no choice but to answer cos she thought there's someone else in the que, the behaviour is appalling. Many times I've put a form in requesting to speak to my doctor I don't get through to her straight away when she's told me many times all I need to do is send her a message when I told her i do she told me she hadn't recieved it, so I started being adamant in my appointment requests that I want to speak to my Dr. I have filled in a feedback form and am still waiting to hear back from Andrew Gee or Lauren, but nothing, I'll probably have better luck getting Lauren to reply back to this post than my feedback form! When it clearly states on the website that if you have a complaint to fill in a feedback form or alternatively call to book an appointment, but when I called I was told the only way was to fill in a form (maybe because they know they can ignore your form!) I have been told to appeal a decision that I hadn't even received in writing, I've asked for a formal letter from them so I can complain to nhs England but still haven't recieved the letter because they don't want me to complain to nhs England or the ombudsman, but I will be going ahead with my complaints.

reviews.author: Polis Sidiropoulos
reviews.text: Incompetent manager and staff. I have been in this country for 15 years, and this is the first surgery/health center who questions a EU ID card. They welcome new patients but they do make you unwelcome and they are unwilling to help. They will even suggest you go to another GP!!! This was my second visit, I am left without my medication and will definitely look to escalate complaint to the right channels. To be honest, I am scared to meet their doctors now. If you get such service from the admin staff, what could you expect from the medical staff? I would advise for future clients to avoid at all costs. Manager should get the sack and staff must be trained to better serve clients. After all, we do pay our taxes and they get their salary from us. They are here to serve us. If they can't do a simple job like that, then they don't deserve to work in NHS. Any good rating will suggest it was done by one of their staff! We need to take action and try to replace these incompetent people with people who are ready to serve our needs.

reviews.text: Doctors are great! However, even though you constantly ring from surgery opening, it is not guaranteed you'll get through! Then when you eventually get answered an hour later, appointments have all gone! Doesn't matter that you're ill, you can't have one, until next week or wait to go through same process all again over again! The old system was so much better! 4 years on from this review, the surgery has become, not fit for service. I received a text, to make urgent appointment, so I ring, and no appointments available. Ring following morning, as soon as phone lines open, and told I'm 20th in the queue to speak to receptionist. Yeah, right! Not only, have I waited for 2 months for results, I can't get an appointment. I was told at one point, they were delayed, and they would only contact me, if they showed something. I have no faith in any of them, anymore! Even the consultants at the hospital, roll their eyes, at the mention of this surgery, now! It used to be, one of the best. Now it is probably the worst. An update 24th March 2025. Gordon street medical centre is now, no longer taking appointments over the phone or over the reception desk. Told to access on line, by text, with no clear instructions on how? I'm certain there'll be unnecessary deaths, through this total lack of care, and receptionist has put the phone down on me, just for asking her name. My husband has physically approached reception, and has come home with zero help. I will be making official complaint!

So please improve on children's referrals & appointments it's not too much to request, it should just be a speedy check up not a rejected one then accused of not taking my child for help being pressured by 4 people that know nothing about child abuse, quite racist actually when she is naturally fair with dark hair & can't get into a decent sleeping routine or leave the house without me, it's not always appearances all the damage is recorded in the information & should of been passed on to Early Years meeting as they thought I just leave her with no help, I've been requesting help from you for years then the replies are go to the school with these questions how can that be done when they all put safeguarding above everything else, as a child i was severely neglected & abused, I know exaclty what it looks like & others should know aswell how it appears from the outside, so this is one big joke & hopefully, one day the supported well cared for children get all the help they need to manage well through life, things need changing, parent blaming is nothing but delaying & unfair.

reviews.text: I seriously question the purpose of having a GP like this. Every single time I try to see a doctor, it is extremely, extremely, extremely difficult to get an appointment. In the past, they allowed walk-in appointments before 8 a.m., but this was later cancelled. Phone appointments were also available before, and then cancelled as well. They introduced a so-called “new system”, which I tried to use by filling in all the required information, only to be told that it was not possible and that I should make an online phone request instead. When I called the GP surgery again, I was told that this system is only open between 7 a.m. and 11 a.m. As a result, my illness was delayed for over a month and a half, and up to now I still cannot access my GP properly. I even went to other GP practices, but they simply referred me back to my local GP, which is this one. Thinking back on my past experiences, I honestly cannot recall a single time when I successfully booked an appointment and saw a doctor smoothly. On my very first appointment, I clearly booked a face-to-face consultation, but it was changed to a phone consultation without my consent. Because I was at work and missed the call, my appointment was immediately cancelled. When I later went to the surgery in person, I was told that my appointment could not be found in their system at all. I genuinely do not understand whether this GP surgery is functioning properly on a daily basis. In my opinion, the management and organisation are highly unprofessional and incompetent. Additionally, during a previous consultation, I explained to the doctor that I suspected two possible conditions. I then saw the doctor searching for symptoms on Google during the appointment. This made me seriously question the level of professionalism and medical competence. Overall, this has been a deeply frustrating and disappointing experience.

I understand this is preferred but to make it mandatory and cancel an appointment based on this is relentless and shows no empathy at all. reviews.author: Ken Kamdy
reviews.text: A call was initiated to ascertain why an appointment for a mother and child was declined by a GP, providing clinical advice to the service user, and you are not part of the medical team. NHS staff must not unreasonably deny access to services, and patients are entitled to be treated with dignity, receive clear information, and file a formal complaint regarding inadequate care or discourteous conduct. However, a staff member and a receptionist unjustly canceled an appointment, and I have requested the call log. Non-clinical reception staff should not act as if they are GPs; clinical decisions regarding whether a baby or parent requires a review should be made by a qualified health professional (GP, nurse, ANP) following appropriate triage protocols. Professional guidance underscores that healthcare professionals must not unreasonably refuse a patient access to care that addresses their needs and must communicate with kindness and clarity, particularly with vulnerable patients such as parents of very young children. A receptionist informing a practice or service user that she does not consult a GP also provides clinical advice to the service user. Merely asserting that a one-year-old “does not need to see a GP” without a proper clinical evaluation or justification is unlikely to adhere to good practice standards regarding communication and access to care. It is unfortunate that this matter is not being addressed; I intend to escalate this issue further due to the appalling service.

reviews.author: Fiona Simpson
reviews.text: I am always really happy with and satisfied with all interactions with the surgery, and actually recommend it to others. The 2 main doctors and advanced clinician are always very good and are through, listen and take concerns seriously. The patches system is very good and easy to use - myself and spouse have had to use it a few times recently, and we have always then been contacted with an appropriate appointment, if that was face to face, urgent phone, or routine that has always happened quickly. There are some people complaining about lack of appointments etc, I have never found this to be the case. I work in primary care and regularly deal with different GP surgeries, and believe me, simpson medical are one of the better ones!! Perhaps everyone needs to have realistic expectations, and consider that there is high demand for healthcare, which exceeds capacity. The old days of face to face appointments are gone, unless it is necessary this does not happen anymore - often phone calls, including photos etc are often sufficent, and more a more efficient use of staff resources. If a face to face appointment is necessary it will be made whilst anything regarding mental health has always been taking seriously and urgently. I am very happy with being a patient here, and think given the demand they do a good job, and are one of the better surgeries I deal with. Thank you to the staff, I appreciate it

reviews.author: Mark Cole
reviews.text: Good afternoon I would like to give you some feedback on my experience, but I would like to do this in a respectful, fair-minded way. I hope you take it in the spirit in which it is offered. I am a long-standing blood donor. I was unable to donate at my last appointment. because of a low Iron level. Their protocol determined I should have a follow up blood test at my GP. I attempted to book this at the practice but was told it would need to be authorised by the GP, this is understandable. I attempted to do this through PATCHS. The first two days this was not possible as there was no capacity in the system. This was the same on the third day, but then at 12.00 midday I managed to access then system. Not sure when it clears? I assumed the beginning of the day? PATCHS was then excellent, and a blood test authorised within the hour. But attempting to make the appointment was more problematic. 3 days, about 10 attempts, different times of day, on the phone for a total of around 3 hours could not get through. Some of these the automated service said I was first in the que. Based on how long I was waiting I have some doubts about this. In the end I walked to the surgery and made the appointment face to face. There were two receptionists, not unpleasant, but quite “minimalist” in their interactions, empty waiting room, they were not do anything that would have prevented them from answering a phone. Not sure if these are people responsible for incoming calls? Appointment was made, the earliest available was 18 working days. I guess I am lucky it was routine. Having worked in public service, including healthcare for 50 years I do appreciate there are often hidden complexities that the public may not see. But overall impression. Some parts of the system seem to work and some not. Could the donation centre have taken my blood? PATCHS works well when you can access it. Incredibly hard to get through to the GP. Long appointment wait for something that feels very routine and quick to do. When I am seen, based on previous experience I every confidence that it will be efficient and the staff respectful. But it feels it is harder than it should be and with some concentrated thought some opportunities for quick wins here.

reviews.author: Martin Smith
reviews.text: The level of service provided is wholly unacceptable. It is unnecessarily difficult to obtain treatment for even the most straightforward medical issues. Reception staff appear intent on creating barriers rather than facilitating solutions, routinely deflecting requests by insisting patients complete PATCHS forms instead of offering practical assistance. Every enquiry or attempt to seek help is met with the same obstructive response: complete another PATCHS form. I am extremely frustrated with being forced to submit repeated forms, only to receive an inadequate outcome from a GP whom I am unable to speak with directly. When concerns are raised about the quality of care, reception simply reiterates the same dismissive instruction — submit yet another form. To make matters worse, PATCHS forms are not even accessible in the app after a certain time of day, further restricting access to care. This is an inefficient and poorly designed system, upheld by staff who appear disengaged and unhelpful. It gives the strong impression that administrative gatekeeping and cost control are being prioritised over patient care, leaving patients stressed, dissatisfied, and without the timely treatment they require for routine illnesses. Clearly I'm not the only one that's experiencing this poor, unacceptable service as the majority of reviews are of negative experiences and the star rating at the time of this review is less than 2 stars, which is shocking for a community medical practice. Really unacceptable.

reviews.text: If I could post minus scores they would certainly get a minus score. I have a serious condition which is causing me excruciating pain. 9 weeks ago I had an appointment with a doctor from this clinic. Due to no correspondence coming from this surgery other than to fill out surveys from Surveymonkey, I have to call repeatedly. Most times nobody will answer the phone. I cannot go to the hospital as I need a referral from a GP. We wonder why the NHS is in a poor state and underfunded and then look at this clinic and you see your answer. They do not care for you correctly. They allow your condition to deteriorate and do not make the correct referrals to the hospital at the right time . This means that the cost of your care increases massively and the length of time you suffer and the time it takes for you to get well again increases which in turn shortens your life span. They ignore the telephone. The receptionists are rude . They get prescriptions wrong all the time and seems like they alter your prescription without authorisation. The doctors seem to lack knowledge and common sense. The clinic is constantly empty but there are doctors and nurses there and yet they can never give you an appointment. reviews.author: John Mccormack
reviews.text: Only recently moved to this general practice and I regret moving at all. I’d prefer the 40 minute drive to my previous GPs over the below woeful experiences the last several weeks. Attached image of a confirmation text from the GPs. Booked the morning off work, arrive to the appointment to be told I’m booked in for September. Today is Friday the 15th August. Not Monday the 15th September. Secondly, advised over the phone to register my daughter for the GPs I’ll need to come physically into the building to scan a QR code that isn’t on the website. Scanned, completed and registered. Popped in to see if this has progressed as we’ve heard nothing - nothing on the system, come in with your child to register her. Another morning off work. Finally, the biggest disaster - I’ve had a kidney stone for several weeks, agonising pain. Hospital discharged me with a scan booked that due to a motorway accident I couldn’t attend (things happen, life…). I ended up back in hospital again with kidney pain and was advised to raise with my GP to rebook a scan, raised via patches and requested “update via telephone” (though I’m not sure why you’d bother given they’ll either just update in patches with no notification to you or text, they don’t honour the requested means of contact). No update for a week, I log into patches to find the request has been cancelled due to “more information required” from the GP. Bear in mind the request outlines a doctor at the hospital has outlined I require a kidney scan and to request this from the GPs. Symptoms = kidney pain likely stones (not confirmed yet as need the scan, could be more malicious!) and noted worsening pain. I raise another patches request and am advised to come in later that week. At this point I’ve no more tramadol a new born baby and I can’t move. I’ve rang the GP to ask for help, they advised ring 111, I ring 111 who advise speak to the GP. 111 ring the GP who advise they can’t see me today, so I end up back in hospital. With agonising pain. Avoid entirely. I’ll be moving myself, my partner and our child to another GPs that doesn’t have such shocking reviews. And I can see why. One gentleman behind the reception counter is genuinely lovely and helpful, one male doctor (with a slight lisp, apologies on the description but credit due where credit is due his expertise and professionalism were exceptional and I don’t know his name!) the rest of the staff that I have encountered should take note of the above as my experiences have been of incompetence, unhelpful, rude, demeaning and frustrated tones over the phone. Almost as though it’s somehow MY fault information isn’t being passed between health care “professionals” via hospital > GP and / or completed forms disappearing into the void. The reception staff (excluding the outlined gentleman above) are the embodiment of “every GP receptionist thinks they are a medical expert”. This practise would be laughable if it wasn’t a case of people’s lives and welfare at stake. More than embarrassing, an utter disgrace.

reviews.author: Devon Tynan
reviews.text: Shocking GP service. I have been a patient here since being a child, I’m now 24 and only in the last year or 2 has this GP service really gone down hill. My main concern at this GP practice is a fairly new member of reception staff called Farzana, she is extremely rude and unhelpful. I recently rang to review my sons records he had blood tests 6 months prior to this phone call where she told me there was a problem with my sons blood results and I needed to make an appointment with a doctor to discuss these where she offered me an appointment for in 3 weeks time. I went to the GP practice to collect a copy of his blood results so I could see which of his bloods were out of range, when I got there she told me I couldn’t collect my 6 year olds blood results without ID, this is not GP policy you only need ID to collect somebody else’s results if they are over 16. I demanded my sons bloods were reviewed by somebody clinical that day as six months had gone by since the bloods were done. Farzana was extremely argumentative. Another receptionist heard and was helpful and understanding and went and got a nurse to review his bloods. The nurse reassured me and said his bloods had been put as no action by a doctor which was completely different to what Farzana had told me on the phone. Farzana did not apologise for the mistake she had made or the panic and upset she had caused me. A couple of weeks later I had to ring again after my son had been bit by a dog, I asked if she could look if he was up to date with his immunisations so I knew if he was covered for his tetanus vaccine, she told me I would have to wait 2 weeks for a nurse to action this. Here are only 2 examples of how unsafe it is for this woman to work on reception. She makes clinical decisions which I would deem as unsafe and are not within her scope of practice, and overall is a very rude unpleasant person to communicate with. Other than the receptionist, waiting times for appointments are extremely long, the doctor is different every appointment which is unfortunate for patients with long term health problems, also the gp practice appears to no longer be offering blood tests, patients are having to go up to tameside hospital to have their bloods done which can be very time consuming. I have had an ongoing problems with my health since October, each doctor I have seen has given me a different opinion, and I feel I am no closer to a diagnosis. As far as I am aware the NHS is supposed to facilitate informed decision making and involving the patient in their own care something I feel this GP practice does very poorly. I have had to take a lot of time out of work to be treated at the walk in centre due to the lack of care given. I am now unfortunately considering moving GP practice which is a shame as I have been a patient for a long time along with my 3 children and a lot of other extended family members.

Once they received the patients votes to continue running surgery on a permanent basis they scrapped weekend appointments and just went downhill from there. Since the pandemic happened its almost impossible to get face to face for my young baby too, it takes 3 to 4 days of phoning at 8am to even get a phone appointment. After 3 telephone appointments for my under 1 year old In the last 3 weeks I asked for a face to face app today because my baby is not getting better.GP said I can bring baby in within an hour, I tried to explain I need alittle longer but GP didn’t care to hear it she insisted I attend within the hour or baby won’t be seen so I agreed. So when I finally did get a face to face appointment there was 0 flexibility offered which is not good when have other children to get to school. I must say the GP’s and reception staff in general are lovely and GP’s used to be really thorough when seen face to face, but that is unfortunately not the case anymore and the telephone appointments with the GP’s are just pointless and rushed. I will be changing GP, I know the pandemic has put an added pressure on NHS but I can honestly say after 3 years of going from bad to worse Lindley have no excuse for their lack of care & appointments for patients especially the vulnerable elderley patients and young children. I do believe Lindley can return to a really good practice like they once were if patient feedback is taken on board and they actually make changes and manage the practice properly.

reviews.text: I feel this practice is the best example of why the NHS is so stretched and patients have to wait so long for an appointments. They don't seem to follow a good system therefore so many appointments are getting wasted and putting unnecessary pressure on the NHS. I was unable to get an appointment and due to my symptoms was advised to go A&E who done tests and referred me back to my GP for 2 further tests, which were clearly requested on the form so should have been able to book in directly with the nurse for these. The practice couldn't do this, said i needed a routine app with the gp to decide (5 weeks wait) then be referred back to the nurse (within the next 7 days - so 6 weeks minimum). I couldn't wait this long with lower body numbness so visited the walk in (2nd app in NHS) referred for bloods as A&E had advised. I attended the bloods appointment (3rd appointment in NHS) where they were unable to take said bloods which had now been documented as required twice. I was then advised i needed to see another GP to be referred back to the nurse - if I had stayed with this practice that would be 5 appointments, 5 mornings off work (self employed dental therapist so cancelling NHS patients of my own). I registered at a practice on Tuesday and have had my new patient check and the bloods that were requested by A&E within 2 days. Thee nurse at my new practice read the discharge note from A&E and done bloods as it was clearly stated by the Doctor that it was required. Please look into the way you run your practice, I totally understand practice protocols as i have managed a dental practice myself and worked in a GP surgery. The way you operate is ineffective and is straining the NHS therefore inconveniencing your patients. On a positive note i feel all the staff i have met in the short time at the practice have been very nice, pleasent and do try to help there just bound by the lack of appointments of protocols they have to follow

(I was traumatised for years, the NHS minimised this trauma, so did GMC, and I reported too but they failed to act. You're not safe anywhere, and supposedly safe buildings are ideal for predators to work in. Avoid going into appointments on your own if you need something doing. I can't go near most of them now for fear, and many talk down to us anyway while dismissing patients.) This GP also likes to pressure patients ignoring the fact they are fragile, and is the competitive type. Astonishing that they don't understand PTSD and that you can easily worsen the patient's mental health if you are verbally thoughtless. Another thing about this surgery is that the GP's here are not very knowledgeable... I was going in to this surgery coughing non-stop, and they didn't even explore what could have been causing my cough. Well over two years later an open minded respiratory consultant sent me to ENT and we finally discovered that I'd been suffering from LPR for over 2 years. This type of reflux isn't very rare and I'm still shocked that the GP's here didn't even think of this. They would just type "coughing day and night" consistently into my records each time I went into this surgery, and I'd then go home after making no progress. At least I stopped buying useless pills they kept pushing me to buy. Aloe Vera juice worked much better to relieve my symptoms. I'm glad I refused pills for anxiety and depression - they are very bad for the body. Sometimes all doctors do is destroy us.

I explained the situation clearly to the receptionist and asked for it to be relayed to the dentist. Despite this, the dentist showed no empathy or flexibility. After waiting six years to finally register with an NHS dentist since moving to Manchester, I was shocked to be told I would be taken off the register for being late once — something that, having worked in two dental practices myself, I have never known to be standard policy. recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Junaid Ahmed
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: As a long-term patient (diagnosed with a life time illness since 2005) receiving continuous prescriptions and specialized care, I requested a paid private letter confirming the simple, medically accepted fact that chronic stress and hardship trigger flare-ups to my condition. The practice refused the request, claiming "insufficient evidence" a shocking statement considering my two decades as a patient for whom they have continuously prescribed, medication, are informed of my hospital ongoing treatment for years (Vedolizumab, etc.) and liaised with the hospital IBD team. This refusal demonstrates a failure to understand the patient they are treating. Crucially, this contradiction occurred even though I attached an older letter from my specialist consultant where this clinical fact was already written and acknowledged. This extreme administrative obstacle wasted significant time and energy, forcing me to change GPs due to their unwillingness to support a chronic patient.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: JUNAID AHMED
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I was a long-term patient with multiple chronic conditions, including ulcerative colitis, arthritis, and migraines — all of which were regularly managed through prescriptions and hospital treatments. I requested a simple private letter confirming my diagnosis and how stress can affect my condition — something a hospital consultant had previously provided. Despite being willing to pay the £35 fee, the practice refused to provide the letter and didn’t offer an appointment to discuss it. As someone managing serious long-term health issues, I found this response dismissive and lacking in basic patient support. I’ve since moved to a new GP who I hope will be more patient-focused. I’m sharing this to help others understand what kind of support they might — or might not — receive here if they have complex or ongoing health needs. To the management: the decline in care became noticeable after COVID. If you’re genuinely reviewing patient experiences, it may be worth examining the internal changes made during and after the pandemic — because that’s when the ship started sinking.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Lottery appointment system, You need to call between 8am to 8:30am to win a appointment, but everyone else is also calling at the same time. If your call actually connects during this period, congratulations you have a ticket that gets you a 30% chance of an appointment ( providing they have not all been taken already) , if not try the lottery again the next day. You have 1/5 chance for an appointment if you follow my advice. I have a hack for those needing urgent doctor, use all the phones you can get access to and call them one after another, one will likely get through. Edit: It is possible now to go into the doctors before 8 am to obtain a golden ( yellow ) ticket, which helps you bypass the lottery phone system and be seen the same day. While the lottery system is not ideal, I can see its a way to deal with a already struggling health system and therefore I am rating this place higher for finding a way to deal with a failing system. (+2 stars )

This is no fault of the nurses, but the doctors here are completely inept and disorganised, and it’s patients who suffer. The reception staff are mostly useless — there are a few polite, helpful people at the Ladybridge branch, but the rest give off no interest in helping. recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Ellis Birtles
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I have been a patient at this practice for over 10 years and unfortunately the quality of care has declined significantly. I have been suffering with rectal bleeding and recurrent abscesses for several years, and despite repeatedly asking for further investigation, I have consistently been dismissed. Last week I attended the surgery with heavy rectal bleeding. The doctor would not make eye contact, did not offer a chaperone before asking me to lie on the bed with my underwear down, and carried out no proper examination such as pressing on my abdomen. When I tried to explain my symptoms, I was told to leave the room for being “rude”, even though I was in distress. No help was given, and I was simply told to book another appointment six days later. Because of this, I contacted 111 who sent me to the hospital within an hour due to the seriousness of my symptoms. This is not the first time I’ve had to go through 111 or A&E because the practice would not help. Over the years, my abscesses have repeatedly been dismissed as “boils” and I have only been given mild antibiotics. I have now finally seen a dermatologist who believes my symptoms may be linked to inflammatory bowel disease, something I have been worried about for years but the practice refused to investigate. The reception staff often come across rushed and unfriendly, and I leave most interactions feeling patronised and unheard. Even when I raised my concerns with the practice manager, I felt dismissed again. All I want is to be listened to and to receive proper care. After years of pain, worry, and being ignored, I can no longer trust this practice with my health.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Paul Rimmer
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Simply cannot get an appointment to see a GP at this place now. Call in or phone up during the day and you'll be told (politely, in fairness to the receptionist) that there are none available so you'll have to phone them at 8am the next morning. So you call at 8am the next morning, and of course there are dozens of other people doing the same thing. Sit in the queue and you'll be told there are "more than 30" people ahead of you. Wait patiently for 20 minutes, then get cut off. Call back and be told again that there are "more than 30" people ahead of you. If you choose the option to get a call back, they'll send you an SMS with a link to a website where you can see exactly where you are in the queue. I did this the other day and I was 113th in the queue. That's not a typo: one hundred and thirteenth. So that "more than 30" you hear while you wait patiently, could mean there are 31 callers ahead of you, or it could be 112 callers. Or more. Go on the app to book an appointment and, if you're lucky, there'll be one or two available - in a month's time. I guess if you're going to fall ill and need to see a doctor, plan it a month in advance.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I like to share my experience. I had a blood test appointment for my son, we attended the moorgate primary care centre, the rock healthcare first floor. We booked in and had a seat, within couple minutes we had the lovely nurse called, Michelle, call my son name and welcomed us with a beautiful smile. I had forgotten my son cream and labels for the blood test which is applied 1 hours before, I explained my situation to Michelle and she was such a professional and the most gentle person I've ever seen working in a care centre. She arrange a time slot for us to come back and explained how to apply the numbing cream. We came back and we booked in again and Michelle was once again greeting us in with a smile. Really gentle with my boy, he does have autism, and Michelle made me feel entirely at ease, from the bottom of my heart I told her that she made me feel really happy. You are one of the most wonderful person I've ever have met, who take alot care and pride in her profession. Thank you, Michelle x

It was end of day so we were lucky to have a bit more of his time but the whole experience was so positive. We moved to this practice a year ago and I can honestly say the reception team and medical staff have all been so supportive and remember that compassion, empathy and good humour, go such a long way to calm stressed people. Highly recommend.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Faiz ul Haq
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I would like to leave negative feedback regarding Dr. Hussain’s behavior at this surgery. Whenever we ask him for medicine, even for our small children, he always responds by saying: “Go and pick it up from the shelf.” Most recently, my wife, who is pregnant, needed medicine. Whenever she calls, despite the language barrier, Dr. Hussain should at least try to understand that a patient is in need of proper medical advice and prescriptions. Instead, he simply tells her to “get it from the shelf.” I want to ask: if we always have to buy medicine directly from the shelf, then what is the point of having a doctor or a surgery? What role is he fulfilling? During the last call, my wife explained that the medicine he had prescribed previously did not help her at all. She requested an alternative. Instead of listening, Dr. Hussain told her she must not be using the medicine properly. My wife clearly said she knows how to take it, but it was ineffective. At that point, Dr. Hussain disconnected the call and again told her to “buy it from the shelf.” This behavior is extremely unprofessional, dismissive, and rude—especially towards a pregnant woman and parents with small children. A doctor should listen carefully, show empathy, and provide proper medical guidance. Unfortunately, Dr. Hussain’s attitude shows the opposite. I strongly believe that this kind of conduct is unacceptable within the NHS. If doctors are not willing to provide proper medical care and instead simply tell patients to “buy from the shelf,” then they are not fulfilling their responsibility as healthcare providers. I will also be submitting a formal complaint to the NHS regarding this matter. In my opinion, Dr. Hussain should consider retirement, as he does not treat patients with the respect, care, and professionalism that is expected from a doctor.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: margaret miller

For non urgent appointments, these have been offered at alternative times at Moorgate, which is helpful for work purpose. I have seen a few different doctors and each and every one of them has been lovely, efficient and responsive to my needs. They always have time to listen to you and wish you well. I've never felt rushed. The nurses who run the clinics and do bloods etc are so nice, it's good to chat and laugh with them. The office staff are always polite and ready to help if they can. The young man on reception has improved over the last couple of years. It's a good medical centre, though could do with decorating and making it feel a bit more welcoming.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Awful experience this morning at this practice. First of all they thought the best time to do a fire drill would be with a full waiting room and in the freezing cold and rain. Then when we came inside which was 10 minutes after my appointment was meant to be I checked my nhs app to see that my appointment had been changed to 10:45 without my knowledge or notification. There was a reason I booked it at 10:20 not 10:45. I have also never experienced this in the past but I assume it’s so they meet their key performance metrics around access and availability. Some clarity on this would be good and do not blame the fire drill as it was nearly 10 after I should’ve had my appointment when the fire drill was done. Then the nurse I saw basically just fobbed me off when my condition hasn’t improved at all in a week. I have been told to wait another week and come back if it doesn’t improve despite already waiting before I came in to see someone in the first place.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Today,on 18 February, I had the privilege to have phone appointment with Ms Fatima regarding my medication and how to improve my health in general.I was amazed the way Fatima interacted with total dedication and professionalism about my on going medical issues.She-listened to my problems and gave clear ,precise solutions.For me it was not just that Fatima was doing her job,infact ,it’s much more than job or duty but I call this as RESPONSIBILITY, which is at a much higher ladder than duty.Keep doing the great work.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Faminah
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I initially wrote a one star review as I got Appalling service by Dr K . This is also not the first occasion this has happened with this specific Dr (infact previously she was one of my favourite GPs especially when it came to children as I felt she was thorough). On this occasion I contacted the gp practice for my son who is under one who had a nose bleed. As a pharmacist I am fully aware of what pharmacy can offer and what knowledge we have and this needed further investigation. Instead of seeing my son she referred the query to pharmacy first for us to only be told this is not an appropriate query for pharmacy first and that my son should be seen by a gp and that this is a red flag. I was completely disheartened by the practice with the constant pushing me to another health care, usually pharmacy or some random resource but my faith has been restored by Sami as a result I have changed my review from a one star to a four star. Sami is an asset to the gp practice, kind and considerate and very polite and professional. I accidentally missed my blood pressure appointment and had the times mixed up and he didn’t make me feel guilty or bad or anything but rather simply booked me in the next day. Thank you Sami!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Megan Lunney
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Had my cervical smear test done at limelight on the 17th of Jan 2026. From the moment I entered the room I felt very at ease and calm. Suli ( the nurse practitioner ) was very likeable, friendly and knowledgeable. She explained what the test was for and reassured any of my worries. I was in the room for no longer than 5 minutes and felt very relieved to have got such an important test done. Suli is an absolute credit to limelight and nurses as a whole…. and the way she advocates for women’s health by simply being so reassuring and respectful at a time that many women feel vulnerable is faultless. Please get your smear tests done! Ask for Suli!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Qasim Akram
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Spoke to a very kind doctor who genuinely cared and supported through illness. She is a credit to Wellbeing Hub and am thankful for her help

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Afroz A
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Absolutely appalling service – avoid Limelight Health at all costs. I was booked a follow-up telephone consultation three weeks in advance. I stayed in all day from 7am, phone in hand, waiting for the call. Nothing. No call, no missed-call notification, no voicemail. When I rang the surgery, I was told the doctor apparently “called twice and I didn’t answer” – completely untrue. The receptionist refused to investigate, offered no apology, and just said “nothing can be done” and “we’ll just go round in circles”. I now have to start the entire process again and wait weeks more for the appointment I should have had. No accountability, no empathy, and what appears to be a falsified clinical record stating calls were made when they weren’t. Patients are being blamed for the surgery’s failures. Reception staff clearly need urgent training and better systems are needed to stop this kind of thing happening. Deeply unhappy and still without the medical follow-up I need. I do not recommend this practice to anyone.

When making a medical or medication enquiry I am always confident my request will be managed effectively. I honestly think this surgery is the best I have used. Importantly and finally ALL the team working at the practice really do CARE! My daughter has now joined the practice and is genuinely happy with the level of care and support.

From the doctors receptionist nurses i couldn't recommended this doctors enough

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Liv Zachariasen
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Keep dismissing me when I contact them when my toddler is poorly They just refer me to a pharmacy that I can't get to. If I want my toddler to be seen, I have to put through a complaint as it's the only way they'll take me seriously and the last time he turned out to have tonsilitis. My requests on AskmyGP just get closed off with a link to a pharmacy. I was never informed I'd have to be seen by a pharmacy first when I registered at this practice and it has never been communicated. They claim you'll be seen sooner, but before this we've always been sble to be seen on the day. I will never understand fobbing off parents who are worried about their small children and I get this every single time now. I have to always push to be seen and when they finally agree, I'm already so upset and stressed by the whole dismissiveness that I can't be bothered speaking to them. Not sure contacting a GP is supposed to trigger anxiety? It's more than reasonable to not rely on a pharmacy for diagnosis, especially for small children!! The last time he had a fever I didn't even bother contacting them as I couldn't be bothered with the thought of being fobbed off with a pharmacy referral. I get that the NHS is stretched and particularly GP practices, but you should be allowed a consultation every once in a while without a battle. I definitely hope nothing serious ever happens to myself or my family or we better hope the pharmacy can treat us. However having seen the pharmacist as they told me to, I'm none the wiser so what an absolute waste of people's time and energy to pass them round such a useless and inefficient circus. So disappointed as they have resorted to such a lazy way of dealing with their patients.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Had great service , used My GP to explain problem had call back a few hours later from, Marco the trainer ACP , absolutely brilliant , sorted my problem quickly , gave good advice and thing improved over the next couple of days , Ashville gives the best GP service I have had, keep on doing what your doing you are truly amazing people

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Shereen Simmonds
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Awful experience. Taken me off the database because I’ve moved from the area, even though I work 5 minutes away. I expressed that I would struggle changing gps because of underlying issues and they didn’t show any empathy. I expressed that my dentist etc were still in Manchester, as I am physically unavailable through the week to attend any appointments, working 6am until 8pm Monday to Friday. I stated that I’d had an ongoing condition, knew what it was but they had to test me. The first test they lost, the 2nd test they tested for the incorrect issue, the third they said I didn’t have what I thought. When I was referred to a specialist they confirmed on the day (within minutes of being tested) that I did in fact have what I initially thought! My family member used a doctor here when she was extremely depressed. When they asked what was wrong with her, she expressed that she didn’t know, to which they replied, “well if you don’t know how am I supposed to know.” For someone who was vulnerable at the time, that isn’t what you’d expect to be said from a health care professional. I believe if she wasn’t as strong as she was, just may have tried something unthinkable. When I sent a letter of complaint nothing was done. The doctors name is Dr Hoddes! They misdiagnose people, give them antibiotics or painkillers and they end up dying of cancer. Avoid at all costs!!!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: See See
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: If you want to die, not get referred or seen, visit this GP surgery!!! A family member visited this surgery on several occasions with stomach pains and weight loss. This GP surgery fobbed her off with painkillers and antibiotics. My relative collapsed at home, ended up in hospital via ambulance requiring 4 units of blood because of a burst ulcer. Another family member has had chest issues, she's been wheezing for months and the GP only prescribed her with antibiotics over and over again. No referral to find out what's happening. A friend is suffering from chronic pain in her leg due to having surgery. All they have prescribed her is co-codamol. She needs something stronger but can't get an appointment. The staff here are also rude. They have no compassion, come across as patronising and have no respect, especially the reception staff. As some have mentioned the staff are good, it makes me wonder if this GP surgery has it's prejudices. The only good respectable doctor they had was Dr Beresford and he retired. This surgery needs closing down. If I could give a zero star rating, I would.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Oj B
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: It's so heartbreaking to see this practice degenerate to this level. How hard can it be for people to be nice and professional? They have a lot to do in terms of training all their staff. And I mean ALL of them! From people's skills to civility, mannerisms, tone of voice when addressing patients and how to approach to patients who are already suffering. I've had so many unpleasant encounters with them that I don't want to mention. They make it look like they are doing a favour by attending to you. So appalling! They soon will be having no stars whatsoever if they don't make proper and needed adjustments on their people's skills. It really is appalling! Yelling at patients!! 9/03/2026 I can't believe that I am back here after 4 years to leave a very negative review of this establishment. Before, I go any further - I want to make it clear that, whatever issues patients are having with this medical centre are 90 to 95% front desk, admin, nurses and lesser staff (sorry, for lack of a better word to use.) The Dr's are unaware of the front desk, admin, and lesser staff issues - and yet bear the brunt of the end of the stick should the establishment suffer. I've had very unbelievable and excrutiatingly painful experiences with them from the beginning of this year. In short, (they put up lies and mark your profile, including your number should you call and then mete you undeserved shabby treatment by whoever picks your call, and for whatever reasons best known to them). From the tone of answering your call and how you are responded to is clear and obvious! It is like a syndicate in operation!!! Very evil and unprofessional!!! But we must continue to voice these issues until changes are made, and wrongs are righted. This afternoon I made a call to the centre, having moved to a new home, my daughter who had ran out of medication, due to pressure of moving into a new home and the process of registering with a near gp when settled; called Gorton Medical centre before the weekend to kindly ask for a repeat to be sent to the pharmacy for her to collect. It was not actioned. We called 111 for emergency prescription over the weekend. Today being Monday and on her last tablet, I called the pharmacy to ask if her prescription has come through from the gp, and they said it hadn't. I then called this medical centre to ask why my daughter's prescription had not been actioned and sent to the pharmacy since last week - Knowing she's been on same medication for several years and should not miss days? I was bluntly told by the reception to call back again,(of course, profile marking and syndicate operations in action.) I quickly reminded him how important her medication was, and he should please send it over to the pharmacy for collection. He said he was not in charge of that, and ended up pretending not to understand which medication was needed, (She's only on 1) and is in her profile. To cut the story short, I had no choice but to call 111 again. "Profile marking or spewed lies on the profile" was highly resonant in the voice at the end of the receiver too. I want to clearly state that these issues should be looked into by the right bodies in charge. People are being abused by those that should be providing care, and lives are lost due to these. (I nearly would have lost my life with this centre, cause i was refused care and gp appointment, and was bluntly told to do the worse I can not too long ago.) My daughter was refused duty of care, when she needed, and the excuse was, we had moved homes and was removed by the gp from their system- even when we had not yet registered with another gp. Where is the duty of care? What is the professionalism in this? This is gross misconduct and should be called out. And like I said in the beginning, Dr's are in consulting rooms doing their best and in very high cases are unaware of what goes on at the front desks, admins, and the rest. This types of evil must be called out and put away and far, please.

On one occasion I had a local authority social worker attend an appointment with me as an advocate and to see the challenges I face accessing lawful care. Complain or raise concerns and get told “go elsewhere”. Not a particularly modern thinking practice. Very much the “you don’t look autistic” attitude and “go for a long walk outdoors” when facing a serious MH relapse/crisis. Seem to have the attitude that anything mental health related means you must see the CMHT only and if not under psychiatric care they won’t help you. They don’t feel the need to update medical records despite communication from medical consultants. No excuse for treating vulnerable patients so ineffectually or cruelly.

Like I said when you do manage to speak with a doctor/nurse at the Practice they are brilliant - however some of the booking/reception team do let it down & it becomes very frustrating - especially if you are concerned about an issue. There were further errors - in a similar area but I have bored myself with this already - I’m only writing this because I was asked to & also hope that it can lead to an improvement in the booking system.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: The 5 Brothers Squad
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Benchill Medical Centre is no longer the practice it used to be. All the old doctors are gone, and what’s left is a team that seems to have no urgency, no compassion, and no sense of responsibility. My 12-year-old son developed a serious issue with his eye — it was clearly getting worse — and we spent over two weeks trying to get him seen. I called multiple times, explained that his condition was deteriorating, and still we were ignored. When they finally responded, they didn’t even book an appointment — they just sent us to a pharmacy, where we received no help at all. This isn’t just poor service — this is gross negligence. They failed to provide proper medical care for a child in pain, and they didn’t even follow up. The delay has made things worse, and we’ve had to seek help elsewhere. No examination, no urgency, no care. This practice has changed for the worse — it is now unsafe and unreliable. If you value your family’s health, especially your children’s, I strongly advise you to go elsewhere.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Used to love this practice, the doctors and staff were brilliant, but many have left now. The new appointment booking system is awful. It is impossible to book a non-urgent appointment, with a specific doctor at a time that suits you. This means if you would like a follow up or review appointment, you have to know what days your doctor works, remember to fill in the form on that morning (before they reach capacity) and hope that the appointment you are given fits in with your schedule. Really not good if you work and/or have a chronic condition.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: SUSAN HAMPSON

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Amrit Kaur Swalley
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: During my call, I was advised by reception staff that I should take my mother to the dental hospital instead. This advice appeared to be a medical decision, which I found concerning, as reception staff are not clinically qualified to make such determinations. I later spoke with the reception manager, who confirmed that reception staff are permitted to make these decisions. This is unacceptable and raises serious concerns about patient safety and appropriate triage procedures. In addition, I do not feel that my complaint was handled effectively or taken seriously. There was no reassurance, clear explanation, or appropriate escalation of my concerns. I believe further training is required for reception staff, particularly regarding the limits of their role and the importance of not making or influencing medical decisions. As a patient, I expect clinical advice to be given by a qualified healthcare professional. This matter is particularly concerning given the Care Quality Commission (CQC) requirements, which state that patients must be treated safely, appropriately, and with clear clinical oversight. I trust that this issue will be reviewed promptly to ensure patients are not placed at risk in the future. Thank you

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Alan Shenton

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Spoke to Fiona , the Irish woman who's the Practice MANAGER. Unbelievably rude and someone who seems to not want to go out of her way to help. She constantly talked over my voice and interrupted me , and spoke in a very argumentative and confrontational way......NOT how you would expect a manager in a front of house 'customer service' position to act. I was in hospital in August for an un-related injury , and got to know various staff members and their thoughts about work/NHS etc. I understand and appreciate their workload and resources, and i tip my hat to them. I have a long-standing back injury which is chronic pain every single day. It's badly affecting my life. I have explained this to Dr Chishti and to Fiona , and also emailed and written to surgeons and hospitals. Fiona said i couldn't get a second opinion , after an upsetting and negative letter from a back surgeon i spoke to. WHAT !!. SO NOW I HAVE TO ESCALATE THIS ALL THE WAY.....using my time to maybe contact my local MP , the M.O.D , and the Armed Forces Minister - as I was Medically Discharged and served my country proudly. The saving grace at this Practice is Rachel (and Elamine , who's unfortunately left). Rachel is friendly , has genuine empathy , and is really helpful. Someone who really does go the extra mile. recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Erandi Samaraweera
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: ⚠️ Serious patient safety concerns – I strongly advise de-registering I am writing this review as both a medical doctor and a parent who has been genuinely fearful for their child’s safety while registered at Junction Surgery and Alkrington Surgery. Since registering in August 2025, I have experienced repeated safety and professionalism concerns. My child was once prescribed antibiotics without enough doses to complete the course and I was told that “missing a few doses won’t matter.” This is unsafe advice and only corrected after I insisted. My daughter had a persistent cough for several months and attended multiple times, yet no appropriate referral or timely investigations were arranged. When she later developed fever and blood-stained sputum, an out-of-hours GP was clearly concerned and requested urgent investigations. Despite this, our concerns were dismissed the following day, my child was not properly examined, and I was given incorrect medical information. False reassurance when a child is coughing up blood is unacceptable. When I later requested an urgent private ENT referral due to ongoing bleeding, I was asked to pay a fee during a highly distressing situation, despite previously being told such referrals were not chargeable. The supervising GP did not attend to assess my child in person. Overall, I felt unheard, disrespected, and unsafe. Based on my experience, I would strongly advise patients—especially parents of young children—to seriously consider de-registering and seeking care elsewhere. IF ANYONE NOT TRUSTING ME PLEASE READ THE REVIEWS IN OTHER WEBSITE AND CQC REPORT

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Paris Pinglaux
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I had a 6cm ovarian cyst burst, had internal bleeding, and needed a blood transfusion. I needed urgent surgery. I ended up in A&E - called the GP a day or so later relaying my very worrying symptoms and A&Es findings (projectile vomiting, diarrhoea, unable to keep food/water/tablets down, excruciating pelvic and full body pain, falling in and out of consciousness, blood in urine). A GP told me it was ‘nerves’, and gave no explanation as to why my symptoms suddenly increased tenfold. I was refused anti-sickness tablets many times while dealing with the unbearable nausea and vomiting, because they can become addictive apparently. The pain was unbelievable, I had to take the maximum dosage of cocodamol a day, and that barely touched the sides. Rather than showing concern for the severity of my pain, nausea, and other symptoms, conversations around pain medications became interrogations regarding addiction. I had a large cyst that needed to be removed urgently. They should have heard my symptoms and flagged them as concerning. They should have contacted my NHS surgeon with those concerns, urging them to bring the surgery date forward. They should have spotted the signs and symptoms of a ruptured cyst. Instead of trying to understand what could be happening to cause these very severe symptoms, they did nothing but minimise and ignore my concerns, while refusing me medications that were saving me from ending my life due to the constant, excruciating pain. What exactly are these doctors trained in? How could you be a trained doctor and miss the signs of an ovarian cyst rupture, especially considering my suspected endometriosis? I felt that something was seriously wrong despite this, so I pursued private surgery. If I did not have the means to do that, as many do not, I may not be here now. I could have gone into sepsis, I could have developed blood clots, and god knows what else. Not only that, I also had samples necessary for a referral to gastroenterology go missing three times in a row, which is just bloody odd. I am still in unbelievable amounts of pain, and have ongoing symptoms. I spoke to the practice manager yesterday. I wanted to try to explain how deeply traumatic all of this has been for me. According to her, I should have contacted my surgeon and asked for the surgery to be moved forward, not the GP. Like ???? I didn’t know I had a cyst! That is why I went to my GP for help, so that they could flag this as a potential emergency, justify my concerns, and potentially get my surgery moved forward or flagged as urgent. I am not a doctor, I went to my GP because I had no idea what was going on in my body, I was unbelievably ill, and scared. Is that not what you are supposed to do? However, my concerns were minimised, and I was made to feel dramatic. So, I just kept suffering until I could finally be booked in for a private laparoscopy. I explained that my dad (also at the same practice) has stage four cancer, and recently my brother passed away too, so my mental and physical health are very poor. She wouldn’t let me finish and responded very unprofessionally. I can’t remember her exact words, but it was something along the lines of ‘don’t start that’ or ‘don’t go there’ because her father passed away and she had been through a lot too. Honestly, I was gobsmacked, still am. I don’t understand why she thought it appropriate to respond like that. It is her job, that she is paid for, to be the practice manager. I hoped she would listen to my concerns and understand how negligent the practice had been, but I suppose that would be an admission of guilt. I am 24. I haven’t even managed to graduate university yet because of how much I have had to go through. All I want is to be healthy! I have been living a nightmare, and this practice has only made it harder. The doctors that work there traumatised me. If you do choose to join this practice, ask for doctor Nisha. She is truly lovely. The rest are incompetent.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I had a very distressing experience with Dr Tse Belmond and feel it is important to share this for transparency. I attended an appointment following a panic attack. As English is not my first language, I brought my partner for support. During the consultation, my partner was dismissed and interrupted, and I was pressured to speak despite being visibly distressed. I was prompted to discuss a traumatic experience, which caused me to become extremely upset. Throughout this, I was not offered reassurance or support, and the lack of empathy was noticeable. At a later appointment, I raised concerns about possible Autism and requested an assessment. This was met with a dismissive response, including laughing, and statements were made that Autism is rare in women and predominantly affects men. I found this response unprofessional and not in line with current understanding. I also have concerns about how suicidal thoughts I disclosed were recorded, as they were documented as “depressed mood – minor,” which did not reflect the seriousness of what was discussed. Overall, I left feeling unheard, belittled, and unsafe. I would not feel comfortable seeing this doctor again and would advise others to be cautious.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Gaz W
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Lack of compassion. Lack of professionalism. Lack of empathy. Arrogance. Rudeness. Failing of DPA. Ignorance. This all starts at the reception area. The ladies normally treat their patients like dirt. Very unhelpful with a “tough*” kind of attitude. Every other practice seems to work fine and use common sense, not Silverdale. For some reason you can’t book an appt using the My GP app for Silverdale, but other practices... no problem. You can call after 9am at most practices and book an appt for a GP.... not Silverdale. The poor service then trickles down to the GPs. I feel rushed. I feel things are not explained clearly. I feel they are more interested in hitting targets than curing the sick. Of course it all depends on the GP. I feel some GPs don’t listen to your needs, ailments or feelings and make massive assumptions and with any reason can’t wait to fob you off to a physio or hospital. I have been visiting this practice ALL MY LIFE. It has declined steadily and then rapidly. So after ringing up to book an appt with my GP for a later date, I’ve now been told I need to ring at 8am tomorrow.... WHY??? What difference does it make? Not only was I told this, it’s the arrogance and unhelpful attitude from the jumped up receptionist that is making me seriously consider switch GP. I’d you’re not registered with a practice, don’t bother with this one. It’s very amateur from top to bottom and the care no longer exists towards patients. UPDATE: what a mess. They are changing their system now. I’m certain this joke of a practice is making it deliberately hard for patients to speak to someone or make an appt. They even send texts saying “you have an appt on 02/09 at 2pm, this could be a phone or face to face appt, please contact the surgery for clarification on which it is” - WHY NOT TELL US IN THE TEXT?!? My god, this surgery was better in the 80s before we had computers and apps. I don’t think I’ve seen my GP face to face for 5 years. Absolute joke. UPDATE: after being told Curtis the physio is off sick AGAIN, I was asked to call to rebook an appt. Rang up and said I can’t do the rest of today as going to work. The lady said the nurse will be informed and call me to make an alternate appt. I got the call “we have appointments free all day with a GP” she said, I explained that I’d already said I can’t do this. I did however say, I can make a u turn now and come and see you “oh, we are booked up till 10:30” - the lady literally just told me they had a full free day?!? I eventually settled on 12:30 the following day. My text comes through to say my appt is 4:30pm the following day?!? I’m now sat here at 5pm and still not been seen to. This practice is a farce. No doubt I will get the usual reply from the practice manager where she takes no accountability nor responsibility for how dreadful Silverdale has become.

When I called to make an appointment I have mentioned to the receptionist that I am not sure whether I need a call or a face to face appointment and clearly have stated what my problem is. Which I felt that I have wasted my time because with the pain that I have I could have been seen today and maybe the doctor could see my problem because the pain that I have is not always there. Which means I am not sure when I will get face to face appointment as it’s Thursday today and to get a face to face appointment would be slightly longer (possibly next week) which means I am not sure if I will still be in pain at the time of when I get seen face to face. Now from the time that I was registered at this doctors, until now I was actually thinking that this practice and doctors are very caring towards their patients, I don’t mean by just solving the problems and providing medicine . I defiantly wasn’t asking Dr Cheema about what I expected or about my expectations were, when I see the specialist . This is not what I expect from the doctor at all. We are all humans a despite I have this is an on going problem and still nothing is found and this is not a blame at the GP. There was a lot of warmth and empathy, and when Michelle finished, she introduced me to the younger new receptionist. I said to her take it from me you are learning from one of the best, and from what i observed, that was a master class in customer service. I think we forget that the front line staff in any medical centre, whether it is on the phone or face to face, do an extremely good job, and are faced with a lot of difficulties along the way, and are blamed constantly for things that are beyond their control.
