recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Tracey Fowler
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I, and all my family have been lucky enough to be a patient at Elliott Street Surgery for over 44 years, and the level of care we receive has always been outstanding. It has never failed to be anything less than 100%. I want to express my deepest gratitude to Dr Shah and the team for the outstanding care and support provided lately especially to my Mum following her recent operation when she fell downstairs and broke her Femur bone. When Mum was finally discharged to bed rest at home, from Hospital after a new days, she was complaining that the feet were sore I thought she could be developing bed sores, I called the Surgery at 5.00pm, and the next day at 9.00am a Nurse called to examine Mum when she put us at ease and luckily, it was not bed sores! A week later I was worried about Mum again as her good leg swelled extremely fast at the foot and doubled in size - so I called the Surgery and I was called back within 5 minutes to say the Practice was closing in 30 minutes but Dr Shah would personally visit Mum on his way home and he did within 40 minutes, the door bell rang and Dr Shah was stood waiting to see Mum – I initially thought she had a blood clot in her leg, Dr Shah thoroughly examined her for over 10 minutes and explained things to us in great depth, he explained the swelling could be just because she has had the operation and was bed bound and not able to walk and be mobile, that was one scenario or, it could be water retention and a few other scenarios were discussed too. Dr Shah advised he would send a Nurse to collect Mums bloods the next day to see what the bloods revealed if anything. The next day, sure as his word a nurse attended to see Mum – bloods were taken and sent off. The next day we were called that evening by Dr Shah to say the results had not come back yet and he would call us the next day. That evening a Locum GP Called and said the bloods were elevated and we needed to go for a scan an appointment was made for 2 days later. That day, Dr Shah called to discuss Mums blood results, and I explained what had happened. Anyway, as a precautionary measure, a scan internally and Mum - no clot Dr Shah and all the staff, have always taken the time to listen carefully, explain everything clearly, and make sure we all felt reassured at every stage of Mums recovery. Nothing ever felt rushed and every concern — big or small — was treated with genuine care. It’s rare to find someone who combines medical expertise with such kindness and patience. Thanks to their guidance, my mum has felt safe, supported, and confident throughout her healing process. We are incredibly grateful for the dedication and humanity shown during what could have been a very stressful time. The team ALWAYS go above and beyond to make patients feel heard and supported and welcome, even during busy periods. They are exceedingly compassionate. The Practice is also great for reminding you that you need to see the nurses for check-ups and also medication reviews etc. Another point I wish to make is they have been great with Mum as she has smoked for 68 years, and the Practice now supports her with patches so to my amazement, she has not smoked for over 2 months The reception staff deserve special recognition too. Their kindness sets the tone from the moment you walk through the door. This review seems mainly to be about my Mums care at this difficult chapter in our lives but when I or any of family ever need to see the Doctors, everything is always made so easy with so much empathy. I have never in 44 years experienced anything negative from the Practice. Our Community Practice is a true example of what excellent healthcare should look like. Again, I’m incredibly grateful for the dedication and hard work of the entire team. I would 100% Highly recommended. My final thought… In a time when NHS services are under pressure, this practice stands out as a true asset to the area. I feel fortunate to have such exceptional care right on my doorstep. Thank you, Dr Shah and your Wonderful Team x,

I was sent to get bloods elsewhere and when I attended the appointment I was told that the surgery should have given me some paperwork which they hadn't. I called in on my way home and was told "of course you need paperwork" as though it was my fault. The text they sent confirming the appointment stated I didn't need any paperwork. I wasn't even aware what the test was for as there was no other contact. They recently put me on medication for high blood pressure. Initially, the "GP" I saw put me on a drug which caused my ankles to swell so I asked if it could be changed. Their remote clinical pharmacist changed the drug but when I read the leaflet, it stated that it shouldn't be taken by anyone on anti-fungal medication, which I am. Another drug was prescribed and sent to a different pharmacy. When I went to the pharmacy stated, they said they hadn't got the prescription as it had been sent to another pharmacy which was closed, so I was without the medication for 3 days. I have been sent another appointment with the clinical pharmacist for next week. The times don't fit around my work so I called in to ask for a later call and was refused. Dr Archer agreed I could have a flu jab due my lung condition. An appointment was made for this on the same day I went for a kidney function blood test and I was told I could have it at the same time. The phlebotomist was about to take bloods for a test she had already done about 4 weeks ago until I told her it was a kidney function test and informed her that I had been told that I could have a flu jab at the same time. Her response wasn't good, but suffice to say she didn't do it stating that she was thinking of retiring due to the stress that the admin team were putting her under. I went to reception and was told "no, you can't have a flu jab as you're not old enough". I really do think that this practice has gone downhill which is a great shame as I used to sing the praises of all the staff. I hope Dr Archer reads this and takes some action as some of the staff are rude, ignorant, uncaring and more importantly following unsafe practices. Not what you want from a GP surgery. I am quite willing to discuss things further with him if he wishes to call me. I am currently looking for another practice hoping things will be better there. recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: PC Mumble
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I am updating my review because after speaking to various friends who visit other GP surgeries across Trafford, I appear to be quite lucky with Washway Road. My friends have awful problems getting someone to pick up a phone, they're always number 20+ in the queue, they can't get an appointment. I rarely have to wait to speak to a receptionist, they have some lovely ones who answer the phones these days, very helpful. I have had some very pleasant experiences and interactions with both admin staff and GPs over the last 6 months so I actually cannot complain. The AskMyGP system seems to work well now they have changed it to logging a request between 8 and 10, it's no longer a race to get your request in before it closes/gets full. The on site pharmacist is very good, he can resolve a lot of medication queries so you don't have to wait to see a GP. ******* GPs do not take women's pain seriously. Was ignored and told that 3 periods in a month was absolutely nothing to worry about and was offered a flu jab instead. Completely uninterested so had to go private and seek a second opinion. Currently recovering from a total hysterectomy inc. ovaries and removal of severe stage 4 endometriosis. I also had Adenomyosis. When I wrote to advise them of this, they couldn't even be bothered acknowledging me. This practice has gone totally downhill in the last year or so. Utter disgrace. Edit - it's worth noting this same review was rejected by the NHS website 'because it includes a serious complaint about a specific practice'. So do not trust their NHS review score.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I had a very distressing experience at Medlock Medical Practice. I arrived on time for my blood test and waited as instructed, while several patients who arrived after me were seen first. After over 20 minutes, I calmly approached reception to ask for reassurance, as I was worried I had been forgotten. I am currently receiving treatment for anxiety and depression. Instead of reassurance, I was spoken to harshly and repeatedly called “rude” in front of other patients. English is not my first language, and I believe there was a misunderstanding, but my attempt to explain was dismissed. I was left feeling humiliated and extremely distressed and broke down in tears during my appointment. I would strongly encourage the practice to provide staff with additional training in compassionate communication, mental health awareness, and supporting patients with language barriers. Healthcare settings should feel safe and supportive, especially for vulnerable patients. Unfortunately, that was not my experience.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Honestly can’t fault Medlock, Reception Staff are in the main friendly and helpful (one might have an occasional off day - but don’t we all 🤷‍♀️). Practice Manager very approachable and deals with any small issues swiftly. Dr Pardes is amazing, best GP I have ever had. Saw Dr Arnold today and he was also excellent, took time to explain everything and was very thorough. It’s great to see also that they are training Student Doctors to give same service to future generations. So big thank you to Medlock staff. Would highly recommend.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Louise Gilmartin
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I am a patient at Medlock Medical practice. This past 12 months have been so difficult for me from a medical point of view. Basically I reached 60 and fell apart. For the past few months, I have been treated by Dr Huma Kahlid. I have never had a Dr like her. I feel like I am completely not only listened to but also understood. Dr Khalid has been so amazing, she is truly beautiful inside and out. I actually can’t believe she is going to be leaving us soon. Medlock managers can we not get a petition to keep her with you. From a Woman’s perspective and please don’t take this in anyway than how it is intended, it has been refreshing to have a woman treat me who is so respectful of age and how our body reacts to it. Thank you Dr Khalid so much for your help, understanding and commitment to me as a patient. You will be so missed and a blessing to another practice.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Dawn McGuire
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Made an appointment for 3.10pm yesterday (12th November 2025) arrived at 2.55pm in plenty of time which i always do. Spoke to the receptionist (not sure of her name) she advised me of what waiting room to go to. Half hour after my appointment. I'm still sitting there, watching people come in after me and being seen before me. I didn't want to leave the waiting are as I was on my own, just in case my name was called. 2 hours later (to which I think another patient may have informed the reception desk) I was still there. She asked me to the desk. To my knowledge I was booked in She told me I had been put down as a non attendee. Apologised, then said they had been having problems with the computer system. To which I said obviously not, its the person inputting/working the computer. As I had seen approximately 7-10 people arrive after me and go in before me. So to me that's not a computer error, its a human error. She said I would have to come back tomorrow. I said absolutely not as I work early mornings, and could the doctor see me now as he finishes his shift at 5pm (it was 4.50pm) absolute sham. Luckily, for them to basically save face, I imagine. The doctor said he would see me.

Now the letter is lost and he needs to get a new one again. The whole team is great, very lovely and cooperative whenever there’s a problem, my only problem is with this employee attitude.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I would give less for the stress and anxiety the surgery caused me, but it doesn't seem to let me. If you need care, there is no point going here. The reception staff are lovely however the doctors, nurse practitioner don't seem to care whatsoever ever. In January after a visit to the GP I was given incorrect medication. After the issue was no better I went back, I was told by the GP the 1st GP was wrong. They gave me different medication. After 2 days and getting worse. I presented yo A&E and was kept on for 5nights. Being told each step of the way the GP was wrong. I should have been referred to podiatry on the first visit. The second I should have been sent to hospital... If I followed their guidance any further, I could have lost toes/feet. After hospital admission, I was sensitive to the medication so rang the GP to change it. They advised that technically I don't need medication anymore as I have had a course. Without even seeing me. But I did. That was my treatment plan from my discharge from hospital. This surgery completely exasperate medical conditions unnecessarily. It's almost like doctors don't care anymore.

The care and response from Dr Wilshere was nothing short of excellent and he really took the time to help me with clear and concise advice, additionally preparing a prescription. My medical problem is now alleviated! This surgery has been nothing short of excellent over the years to both myself and my family members. Thank you so much to all the staff for all the hard work, support and care. It is greatly appreciated!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Anish
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I’ve recently joined New Islington Medical Practice as I started to take more responsibility for my health issues, which lingered over the years. I’ve had a 10/10 experience through every consultation and clinician I’ve encountered so far. The facilities are clean and modern, and the reception/back office staff have been very polite and prompt in responses. The new appointment booking system has been very efficient. Having many personal/professional experiences at other GP practices as a GP doctor myself - I have to say New Islington Medical Practice is by far one of the best that I’ve encountered within the region. The waiting times are optimal. I’ve had multiple health issues which have either been resolved or I am now receiving further support for. For sensitive issues, the clinicians are non-judgemental and empathetic in their approach which makes a huge difference. Kudos to Dee and management for their successes thus far and keep up the great work.

I rang today to speak to Dr Zak toon make an appointment and he wasn’t in after I was told the other day that he’s back off his annual leave the staff. recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I've been here for my whole life, I used to give 1 star but I do believe some aspects of the surgery have changed in recent years which is why I changed to a 3. A lot of the doctors here are absolutely lovely and compassionate (especially with mental health) and I cannot fault them on how they have cared for me - for this I would like to give a special mention to Dr Graham and Dr Duncan (this could be due to how recent they qualified as a GP and there now being more awareness of mental health). For anything fertility related Dr Wareing is next to none also! Dr Heron I've struggled with for years due to past experiences and I will not see him, however in pregnancy he has been decent which shows he does take SOME things seriously and is willing to help. The prescription service is very fast and all of my repeats have normally been approved and sent within an hour of requesting. I thought the reception staff had improved over the last year or so however recently they have gone back downhill and are back to being the stereotypical NHS dragons on reception who refuse to help or even acknowledge you past 9.01am when the slots are full - I have even had a GP apologise for this! However it must be said that for me the real star of the show in primrose is Nurse Sharon! She is one of the most kind and compassionate people you could ever meet and I'm sure anyone who has ever crossed paths with her would agree!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I contacted Primrose yesterday 19/11/2024, through askmygp. I told the surgery that I had strained my neck, shoulder and bicep carrying a TV box. I told them that I was in excruciating pain and that I was hardly getting any sleep and asked for help and that I needed to see a doctor and needed some sort of strong prescription medication. I got a call from there reception and told the caller that the pain I was experiencing was unbearable. She said she'd pass it on to 'the doctor' whoever that was supposed to be. Then I got a call back telling me that the 'doctor' wanted me to go for physio. I had politely stated how horrendous the pain was. Got told I'd get a call the following afternoon from their pharmacist. I couldn't go through another 24+ hours suffering this agony. So I went to TGH., walk- in clinic and was seen in & out within 1.5 hours, with strong pain killers and advised on three exercises to carry out. Primrose, in my opinion on this matter we're terrible. No empathy or help for my medical problem from primrose. Very dissatisfied on this occasion.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: If I could give 0 stars if I could. I was born in Urmston and was at Urmston Group Practice til late teenage years, moved around and came back and signed back up. It's not the same doctors surgery that we used to know and love on Church Road. The receptionists need to go on a humility and compassion training course because their actions or there lack of are directly affecting peoples health and mental health. The receptionists also like to try and It seems to be a common theme that one or two of the receptionists (not all) do not seem to have any level of care or sympathy towards their patients. They forced me into crisis because I missed a phone appointment at 18:30 when my appointment was supposed to be 14:45. Apparently they tried to call me twice but number was dead. I know this to be untrue because not only did I not get any notifications that they tried to call but I also have a voicemail as well and they could have left a message. So when I call the next day )which was a friday) to find out what's happened and if I was going to have an appointment then rather than the one that didn't happen the day before. I was met with the usual "you've got to make an appointment, you'll have to call on monday" Despite the fact it was mental health tablets that I needed a review on, for them to use a poor excuse of "it didn't go through" when my phone is connected to wifi calls as well. I was so upset after it all I just told the woman if they aren't going to take me seriously I'll do something serious for them to take notice. No call back, no duty of care, no safeguarding, no making sure I wasn't going to do anything stupid. NOTHING. Then I received a very SNOTTY letter from the practice basically telling me off for saying what I said to the receptionist without even acknowledging that had they of cared or done their jobs, I wouldn't have been in meltdown mode and said what I said. So off the back of that, I have sent a complaint to them TWICE about the whole disgrace of a situation and I have yet to hear from them. Not even an acknowledgement. This review is my last hope that they see this and reply to me because if they don't then I'm going to go above their heads as it's becoming a joke at this point. Business are expected to acknowledge a complaint within 3 days and set out within that acknowledgement a time frame of when I should hear back from them. It's been months.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Humairaa Ahmed
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Had an appointment today at 11:40 for an ultrasound scan which I had to have a full bladder for. I took a taxi to the place but as the taxi driver went the wrong way, by the time I got through to the centre was 11:43 and I explained to the receptionist that I’ll be 5 minutes. She said that was fine. I arrived at 11:50 and sat in the waiting area waiting for my ultrasound. When I arrived, was only 1 woman I saw go in and come out 10 minutes later. After that it was just me sitting there waiting. Nearly 20 minutes had gone by so I ask the receptionist. She said I am half an hour late and how I said I’ll be 5 minutes and that they won’t see me , even though I walked in passed reception at 11:50 to sit in the waiting area which was by the ultrasound scan room. I explained myself. Then she said okay just continue waiting. 25 minutes later the person at the ultrasound came out for me and explained how I’m too late and she can’t fit me in. Even though I’m the only one there and have been for the past 35 minutes. She said she’s been calling for me. No one called for me at all whilst I was there. Whatever I was telling her wasn’t going through to her at all. So after sitting there for nearly 45 minutes on a full bladder that I’ve had for 2 hours, I got sent home and a phone call after to re arrange. No thanks I would rather not have the scan anymore to find the issue of what’s making me ill rather than dealing with people like this. And bare in mind whilst I was waiting, one woman kept coming in and out of the room ‘checking around’ but never called my name or spoke to me. Wish I could give this place 0 stars

If you want names- Dr Lyburn is extremely rude, condescending and just generally vile. Dr Badesha literally laughed at me over my skin problems. All the good doctors like Dr Ash seem to leave the practice. Most of the receptionist staff are extremely rude, then do their best to block you from making complaints. One of them tried to force me to give a personal reason for my visit to the GP and when I refused, I was refused an appointment. I was then gaslit by two reception staff over what happened. But I know for a fact phone calls are recorded so maybe they should start listening back to them if there is any confusion in their minds about what has happened. The practice constantly mess me around with my medication, saying they haven't received emails from my mental health team when they have clearly been sent. I have been left without medication and left on too low of a dose because of this. I will say the nurses are lovely and I don't take issue with any of them but unfortunately this isn't enough for me to stay at Sorrel Bank. Please find a different doctors practice if you are considering registering with this one, it's not worth it. I have to phone monthly to chase this up with the reception team and I get a response that it has not been requested and they will put through now and will take another 48 hours. I am being left without the insulin for a day or 2 and this is becoming a concern. I have raised a concern in the last month and I got attitude from the ‘assistant manger’ which i find her approach very unprofessional and like she doesn’t want to be bothered. The practice manager is never on site to raise a complaint to and told to put in writing which I have and never got a reply from Patrick neither. I did so, but I still did not hear back from them after another two to three weeks. When I contacted them again, they said that my records had been misplaced. I then submitted my records online, but it has been almost three months and I have still not heard back from them. recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Michael Higham
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: 12 months ago I tried 3 days on the trot to get an appointment because I'm having difficulty breathing, especially when I'm laying down. After the 3d try i give up. I am now 65 years old and things have got worse, but I still can not get an appointment. Doctor Perkins is a lovely man. But I can not help wounder how many people have died unnecessarily because there condition was not diagnosed early enough. You need to go back to the old way of making appointments (before Covid) because early detection is crucial.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: picdriver
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Have been with Dr Perkins (Brian) since he took over from Dr Peel (old practice?) for well over 20 years. Very easy going & friendly & listens to you. Obviously he has time slots but you never feel rushed. I understand the frustrations & one stars regarding trying to book an appointment but this seems to be across the board now as opposed to it being solely an issue with this particular practice since covid. When you do get through to book an appointment you're greeted with a not so happy receptionist who makes you feel like a burdon on her day. I try & put this down to dealing with all the phonecalls first thing of a morning! Otherwise she's been very accommodating & helpfulI when the need arises. I don't like having to tell a receptionist what my issue is though...It should be between me & the doc. Paula the nurse was equally great & also had time for questions etc. A nurse I saw on an earlier visit was terrible...she couldn't wait to get rid...had no time...& the waiting room was practically empty! ..she didn't know why I was there! (health check). But overall no intentions of changing doctor....proper family doctor to us for many years. If I knew I was going to write a review this long I'd have sold it as a book...donations instead are welcome.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: ENGLISH WITH SABBIR
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Terrible Experience at NHS GP Practice The Absolute Worst I am writing this review to express my extreme dissatisfaction with Dr. Parkin's NHS GP practice. This practice is, without a doubt, the worst healthcare experience I've ever had. Here's a list of my grievances: Unbelievably Long Wait Times: Getting an appointment is a nightmare. Even after securing one, expect to wait in the waiting room. Unprofessional Doctors: I've had appointments with various doctors , and none have instilled confidence. They seem unconcerned about my health problems. I would recommend looking for alternative GP practices in the area. There must be better options out there with qualified professionals who genuinely care about their patients' well-being. If you're looking for a GP experience that will leave you feeling more unwell than when you arrived, then NHS is the place for you! Buckle up, because this is a tale of woe. Getting There is an Odyssey: Firstly, reaching a human to book an appointment is an act of pure masochism. The phone lines are permanently engaged in a game of dial tone torture, and the online system is about as user-friendly as a medieval trebuchet. Finally, you're ushered into the office. Prepare for a five-minute consultation. Don't expect in-depth examinations or thoughtful diagnoses. Here, a generic prescription pad are your only companions. I understand that the NHS is under a lot of strain, but that doesn't excuse the unprofessional and unacceptable service.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Amelia A
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I brought my daughter for an appointment and we were kept waiting 30 minutes past our scheduled time. When we were finally called in, we were then left to stand in silence for another 5 minutes while doctor Hassan typed notes from previous patients. While still typing and without making eye contact or examining my daughter, he asked why we were there. When I explained it was for a spot on her leg and that she’d had it for a few months, he immediately made a judgment and said it “must not be much of an issue” if we’d waited that long. He also commented that “they will ask why you haven’t brought her in for months” without explaining who “they” were, and before he had even looked at the spot. Only after making these remarks did he finally examine her leg and then told us it wasn’t serious and to return in two weeks with warm compresses. My concern isn’t the medical advice itself it’s the rude, dismissive, and judgmental manner, particularly when speaking to a parent about their child. Unfortunately, this is not an isolated experience. We have experienced similar rudeness from this doctor on multiple occasions. Between the repeated unprofessional behaviour, poor communication, and lack of respect for patients’ time, this is not a practice I feel comfortable bringing my children to, and I would not recommend it to other parents.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: L B
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: GP's and Nurses are brilliant. Always friendly and easy to talk to. Both nurses I've seen there have been bubbly, happy and chatty and put me at ease, even when having a cervical screening :') One of the reception staff comes across very rude on the phone at times which isn't great when you're ringing up about mental health issues. She has at other times when I've physically been in the surgery been fantastic and extremely helpful. I can sympathise with them to an extent as they must get a lot of abuse but it shouldn't be pushed onto others. When you're physically in the building though they're all spot on. Struggle to get through and get appointments if you don't keep trying to ring at 08:00. They do seem to have introduced a phone queuing system which helps massively. With there only being a limited amount of appointments I think the reception staff need to be firmer in turning time wasters away and directing them to the correct place (pharmacy/a&e/self care). Also, they should tell people who repeatedly don't attend their appointments and dont have the decency to advise reception they will be struck off if they don't have a valid reason. Surgery is bright, airy and clean. Chairs could do with being spread out a bit more in my opinion but I'm claustrophobic so perhaps a bit biased. Overall, best doctors surgery I've been too in Heywood and I would recommend. All surgeries seem equally difficult to get appointments so can't hold that against them. As for the occasionally rude receptionist, this is just my experience and how I perceive something that's been said and that will differ from person to person. We all have bad days, we're only human :)

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I saw Dr Shibeika in July and August What a lovely GP! He was patient, understanding, didn’t rush me at all, and had time to listen to me, unlike others within the practice. One thing I thoroughly disagree with, is being rushed by a GP (we shouldn’t all be classed as time/wasters!) He carried out tests and was very reassuring, that I would be ok. I was sad to hear he was temporary and leaving at the end of August. I had to have some more tests, and knew I’d be seeing someone else for my results 😟 However, to my delight, when I made the appointment for October, Dr Shibeika was available 👍🏻 When I saw him this week, I said it was great to see him. recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I am extremely disappointed with this practice. The practice also fails to respond properly to complaints, leaving parents without answers or accountability. I have also personally experienced significant delays and poor communication when trying to get urgent care and test results. Repeated failures like this put patients’ health at risk. I cannot recommend this practice to anyone who expects safe, timely, and responsive care

The waiting time for an appointment is over a month, which is unacceptable, and every interaction I have had with this practice has been unsatisfactory. At my first appointment, I had recently lost my baby during pregnancy. The doctor showed little concern and what felt like thy continued writing up previous consultations during my appointment. I was issued a sick note and sent on my way .I left the appointment feeling worse than when I arrived. I was later referred for further care however, this referral was not completed for several months because the doctor was reportedly off sick and no alternative arrangements were made. I find this particularly concerning, as I received a message from the receptionist regarding the referral shortly after the initial appointment, yet no action followed. Overall, the lack of compassion, poor communication, and delays in care have been distressing. I would strongly advise anyone who needs medical support to consider a different practice. My experience has been extremely disappointing. I will be changing doctors ASAP .

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Martha Beatriz Potter
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I'm writing this review as a frustrated patient who's had a shocking experience with this practice's service. I phoned at 8am and waited 25-30 minutes just to get an answer. I explained my situation - my consultant had asked them to prescribe more antibiotics for my lung disease, which makes any cold or flu linger and often leads to infections, making me cough uncontrollably and causing incontinence. It's a nightmare. The response seemed straightforward when I spoke to them, but then I got a call an hour later saying I needed to fill in an online form to be triaged. A nice lady helped me with this, but then... nothing. I phoned again at 2pm, was told they'd contact me, and... crickets. It's now 6:47pm. The worst part? This isn't the first time this has happened. I've ended up in A&E twice because their system is so appalling, and both times I've been told "this is something the GP deals with". I rarely use their service, but when I do, it's usually to be told to go to A&E or a walk-in centre. It's infuriating. To anyone considering using this practice, be warned: their system is broken, and it might end up costing you a trip to hospital. Not exactly what you want when you're already feeling well.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Barry
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Having recently had a medical issue whilst abroad I was advised to contact my Medical Practice at home. I have been a patient at Greenbank since the 1960s fortunately I have not had to attend on a regular basis however I was pleased to be given a prompt appointment and saw a doctor who was most pleasant and professional and was able to fully interpret the advice I had received whilst abroad. She arranged for me to have an ECG which was done within a week at Greenbank by an equally pleasant and professional person. The results of the ECG were conveyed to me later that day by the the doctor who saw me initiallly and she organised for me to see a specialist at Oldham Hospital within days. I remember that a few years ago I read in the local paper a review of the Greenbank Practice which was rather poor, however after contacting Greenbank I was given the opportunity, a few weeks later, to meet with the leader of the group who had produced that report which illustrated how easy it is to criticise particularly over petty issues. The second follow up report a few months later recognised the true value of the Greenbank practice and the practice was marked up as Good. I have also had recent visits to see the physio at Greenbank with my slight hip problem and again I received prompt and professional help. My golf is just as bad however my hip is on the mend.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: R Ku
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I visited the practice today to make a simple enquiry, and unfortunately my experience with one of the reception staff in person was very disappointing. While telephone interactions are usually polite, the face-to-face communication I received today felt dismissive and unnecessarily abrupt. Patients come to the practice because they are unwell and genuinely need support, not to feel uncomfortable or spoken to in an unprofessional manner. Respectful communication is a basic expectation in any healthcare setting, and it is essential that staff members are able to respond to patients’ questions with patience and courtesy. I hope the practice will review its customer-service standards and ensure that all staff are placed in roles that align with their ability to support patients appropriately. Improving front-desk communication would make a significant difference to the overall patient experience.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: J
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Very poor experience overall. I was referred by my GP for some tests and given a 6:00pm appointment, which meant taking the afternoon off work. I arrived early to the appointment, but the staff appeared to be preparing to close, despite the clinic not due to shut for another 30 minutes. The lights were off and cleaning staff were already present. When I explained that I had an appointment, the staff seemed confused and told me there were no appointments left for the day. I was questioned in a rather patronising manner about whether I was in the correct place or had the right day, but no one asked for my name or referral details, which surely would have been the most basic step in checking their system and clarifying the situation. I was ultimately turned away without any attempt to investigate further. I contacted my GP the next morning and they confirmed that the appointment had been correctly booked. I am unclear what went wrong, but it is frustrating to now have to rearrange the appointment and potentially take additional time off work.

Every time I raise a health concern they are just absolutely not interested. I went to seek help with heavy periods. DR Saraf just looked at me and said "what do you want me to do about it?" in the most condescending way possible. Her solution then was to put me on a mini pill. Without once checking my blood pressure before prescribing it or at any point during the 10 months I was on it. Result? I now have to take blood pressure medication for the rest of my life, it's affected my vision and I will need to see a cardiologist once a year for a foreseeable future. Are these meds being reviewed to make sure they are working? Of course not! I also have iron deficiency, due to the heavy periods. Was promised regular blood tests to make sure the levels stay in range. Upon the last request to have them checked I've just had the answer of "they were fine 5 months ago so no need to check" when I had clearly stated I'm getting the same symptoms as the time before when they were extremely low! Communication? Well, now you submit an online form to get an appointment. So far I've submitted 3. 2 got completely no reply. And the 3rd one featured a generic link with no option to respond or raise any further concerns. I could go on about the lack of care and unprofessional attitude, but I genuinely don't believe they will change anything. To anyone considering joining this GP practice, just don't. Might do more harm to your health than good as it's been in my personal experience!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: As I approach my 79th summer, I seem to pop more pills than a 1960’s Rolling Stones roadie. Which takes quite a bit of organising in terms of ordering them from my local surgery to keep the supply line flowing. When it comes to being business-like in such matters, on a scale of 1-10, one being chaotic and ten being hyper-efficient, I probably clock in at something like minus 5. That is in contrast to the present Mrs Gardner, who could probably re-organise Manchester United in the morning and the England cricket team in the afternoon. Anyway, the New Year being what it was, I thought I had ordered two sets of tablets from Leesbrook surgery at the dawn of 2026 when the evidence indicates that, in point of fact, I hadn’t. Doh! When this dawned on me earlier today, panic set in for I had consumed my very last Solifenacin tablet last night. We are warned to give plenty of notice when re-ordering prescriptions, particularly at this time of year when the whole NHS is so stretched. So imagine my surprise, delight and admiration when my hasty message to Leesbrook surgery was answered immediately. Together with the ever helpful staff at Well Pharmacy, they arranged for me to have the required medication in my hands this very afternoon. Thank you once again for your brilliant service. Happy New Year from John Gardner

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I appreciate that GP services are incredibly stretched and it can be very difficult to balance offering in advance routine appointments with more urgent on the day appointments. I think this surgery, however, is striking the balance well. The last 3 times I’ve required fairly urgently assessing, I was seen on the same day and treated. Early on this year, after a bout of pneumonia, I suffered a follow up chest infection. I was seen the same day, prescribed antibiotics and the doctor sent a sample from my chest off for testing. I got a call a few days later saying the bacteria on my chest wasn’t the commonly found one and as such would not respond to the antibiotics I was given and he had sent a new prescription to the pharmacy. So instead of seeing me, prescribing something and leaving me to it, the Doctor has followed up, sought more information and then realised my treatment would need changing. Despite the huge time constraints they’re under, they’re still doing a thorough job. I was again recently seen the same day with another potentially urgent requirement. The surgery also now accepts appointment request forms - categorised as urgent and non urgent so you don’t have to wait on the phone. Trying to get through on the phones can be frustrating for sure. But this is, in my view, a Solid example of a clinic that does the best with the resources it has, despite huge patient loads. And doesn’t cut corners on healthcare just to save time. Thorough, understanding and incredibly hard working is my experience of the admin and medical staff I’ve encountered here.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Michael Keating
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I felt that my health problems were dismissed and was disappointed and frustrated with the consultation overall. I had registered with the surgery for the GP to consider shared care protocol for ADHD medication prescribed and monitored by a private company I have paid for monthly since January 2025. I'd been advised by the receptionist prior to registering that this would at the least be considered. During my first consultation I was told indefinitely that the practice had a 'blanket rule' against prescribing in this manner. I would have accepted that, as I did with my previous practice, however I feel I was then delivered misinformation that was disheartening and upsetting. The GP told me that 'these private companies will give anybody a diagnosis of ADHD', something which I feel particularly upset and frustrated by. I know for a fact, as a specialist nurse for psychiatry working in primary care that there are many people referred for an ADHD assessment that are not diagnosed but offered alternatives and private companies will make recommendations based on valuable assessments that patients benefit from regardless. For a medical professional to deliver this false information can be especially damaging to somebody in my position, having waited years and paid excessively for support with. I, like many other service users have found relief and in the very least been validated by a diagnosis of ADHD which has answered a lot of questions and provided a pathway to improved wellbeing and hope for the future. The GP also stated that these private companies do not offer a true 'shared care' approach, and that if there are any problems with prescribing in primary care there is no support available from them. I know that this is also false as I have been instructed to remain under the care of the private company and pay for six monthly reviews from the specialists working alongside primary services to ensure safe prescribing and management of medications. The GP also attempted to misinform me that private companies prescribe medications without ensuring safe titration and effective physical health monitoring. Again, I know for a fact that I was sufficiently monitored in terms of bloods, ECG and regular blood pressure and weight reviews since being diagnosed with ADHD in January 2025. In summary, I feel Albion Medical Group have been negligent and failed to deliver individualised care based on service user need. Not only that, but many of the false statements assumed by the GP could have been particularly damaging to vulnerable people with a diagnosis of ADHD, further marginalising people like myself trying to seek support for this disability. If the surgery have a 'blanket rule' against considering shared care protocols for ADHD medication, they should at least ensure the GP's are better informed and work harder not to further dismiss and discredit patients already struggling to access safe support and guidance.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Ali Channa
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I have never experienced such an unprofessional and shocking service from any GP practice in my life. Little Town Medical Practice is an absolute joke. We booked an appointment and had to wait three weeks just to be seen – that alone is ridiculous. When I finally arrived for my appointment, I signed in and waited 40–50 minutes past the scheduled time. I became impatient because the appointment time had clearly passed. I asked the receptionist, who told me to “wait another 5–10 minutes and the doctor will see you soon.” After waiting another 10 minutes, she then told me I needed to come back four hours later at 3:30pm. What a joke. I had children to pick up from school, so attending four hours later was impossible. I asked if I could be booked in for the following week instead, and I was told they had no availability at all for the next two weeks. Completely unacceptable and honestly disgusting. To make matters worse, while I was there another patient was arguing with staff because the doctor refused to see her child despite them having an appointment as well. That alone shows this GP treats multiple patients the same way. This is not the first bad experience either. On previous occasions the staff have been extremely rude. When complaining over the phone in the past, I was told things like: “Why don’t you change GP?” “Why don’t you move out of Oldham?” Disgusting attitude. Completely unprofessional. Shows clearly that this GP surgery does not care at all about its patients. Little Town Medical Practice needs serious improvement. People rely on their GP for their health and wellbeing, and this kind of treatment is shameful. I would not recommend this surgery to anyone.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I received a message from the practice asking me to contact them, but it is virtually impossible to reach them. I have called repeatedly throughout the day, and the call either rings out or ends automatically. This isn’t a one-off issue—mornings are no better when you actually need an appointment. It’s now half past one in the afternoon, and still no answer. If patients are expected to respond promptly, the practice needs to be accessible. At this point, it’s genuinely frustrating and unacceptable. What exactly does it take to get through to someone? Thank you for your response. I appreciate the explanation regarding staffing issues and the previous callback problem. However, I would like to clarify that my concern was not about expecting to “get straight through in the morning.” My concern was about repeated attempts throughout the day, including the afternoon, where calls either rang out or disconnected automatically. Being asked to contact the practice and then being unable to do so is understandably frustrating. Patients are not expecting special treatment — simply reasonable accessibility, particularly when prompted to make contact. I hope that moving forward the focus remains on improving accessibility rather than questioning patient expectations. Kind regards,Natasha

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Ayanna
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I am writing to formally raise serious concerns about the continued poor standard of care and service I have experienced at your practice, which has now reached an unacceptable level. I had a telephone appointment scheduled for today at 10:00 AM to discuss blood test results I have been waiting over two weeks for. The doctor called but let the phone ring for barely a second—so briefly that my phone did not even make a sound before the call ended. This happened twice. By the time I looked at my screen, both calls had already disconnected. It appears these calls were made purely to be logged as “missed” without any genuine effort to reach me. This is not the first time this has happened. During my previous set of blood tests, I experienced the exact same issue with the same doctor. It is becoming a pattern, and I feel unfairly blamed for missing calls that I was never given a fair chance to answer. I contacted reception immediately after the missed calls and was told by one receptionist that the doctor would call me again by 3:00 PM. I waited all afternoon and received no call. When I followed up again, a different receptionist informed me that I would now need to wait until Monday to rebook the appointment. This lack of consistency and the conflicting information from staff is extremely frustrating and unprofessional. Had I been advised at the time of my first call this morning that it was unlikely I would receive a call back, I would have rescheduled immediately while appointments were still available. Instead, I have been left waiting all day, only to be told I now need to start the process again next week. This entire experience follows an already distressing and, frankly, concerning blood test appointment. During the test, the nurse attempted to draw blood from my left arm but was unsuccessful. She then inserted the same needle into my right arm, again unsuccessfully, and a third time into another site using the same needle. I was left with severe bruising due to how aggressive the procedure was. Afterwards, I looked into this and was shocked to learn that reusing the same needle for multiple injection sites is not in line with health and safety regulations. I find it deeply troubling that this occurred, and it has left me feeling not only physically hurt but also incredibly unsafe in your care. All of this is part of a larger issue I have faced at this practice: I have repeatedly had to fight to have my symptoms taken seriously, and even getting basic follow-up care feels like a battle. The reception staff regularly provide conflicting, inaccurate, or vague advice, which only adds to the confusion and stress. At this point, I feel neglected and disrespected as a patient. I will be looking into registering with another GP practice, as I feel the standard of care at this one has significantly declined during my time here. I hope this matter is taken seriously, as it relates not just to poor service, but to potential breaches in clinical safety and patient care standards

I spent years struggling with my mental health and not feeling properly understood in the past, but Dr Galvis approaches care in a truly thoughtful and creative way. I have always got through to the practice and have managed to get an appointment 99% of the time. Reception staff have been helpful and friendly. I have always been treated with courtesy and dignity having a long-term condition. I do think people should be realistic. Use the pharmacy or 111 for advice. Urgent problems go to ED. recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: On a first visit to this Cheadle Hulme site (having registered at the southern GP site in Handforth) we found some of the internal signage confusing. This practice is split across two sites but does not always show the road name (or even the postcode). Assuming that "everyone knows" might not be the best approach to successful communication with your customers. Just the first visit ever, early in September 2025.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Aniq Choudhury
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I have waited for a month for my GP to write me a supporting document about my mental health as he is the only one who knows my history well but I have received nothing and when I call the practice, I get the same excuses all the time. recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Brian Timperley
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: It's nice to be dealt with when your issue is time relevant- not sorted yet but at least on a path way It's those stories where people are either without diagnosis or pass away waiting!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Mike Andrews
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Always receive very good service

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: dominic creighton
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Incredibly thoughtful and considerate doctors, really impressed with the four Ive had appointments with this last couple of years. They would all get five stars. However - the receptionist I dealt with yesterday, on my phonecall, with regard to a potential life threatening emergency, was AWFUL. One Star. Less to be honest. Rude, brisk, dismissive, uncaring, and absolutely a disgrace to the Medical Group, and the brilliant, professional doctors who actually work there. If I wasn't a stubborn man and really pushed this receptionist on my phonecall for my (absolutely necessary) emergency appointment, I wouldn't have been seen. It's appalling to think this receptionist could be responsible for potentially seriously ill people being ignored and dismissed. I wish there was some way of lodging a formal complaint but not sure how to go about it. And again, the doctors? Brilliant! Can't recommend enough 😊

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Last Week.
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Physio Steven Barrett. “On it !! ” Steven is a fantastic attribute to Cheadle Hulme Medical Practice. His qualities are. Respectful, Caring, Patient, and Persistent. Stephen, leaves no stone unturned. I have nothing but faith in his capabilities. We are very, very lucky to have him! THANK YOU 🙏🏻

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: maria spence
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Been with this practice over 45 years but feel the waiting room is disgusting,the chairs are filthy and full of bacteria,surely the staff can see this so why hasn't anyone addressed this issue.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Danielle Ashcroft
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I've nothing but positive experiences with this surgery so far. I've received same day appointments and been seen by caring and empathetic medical professionals. It's an adjustment to have to use the website to submit requests, especially when I'd prefer to speak to a person, but I've found the teams response to requests pretty swift. I haven't experienced any of the negativity cited in other poor reviews.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Eileen Clifford
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I have had an appointment today. My care once again from this practice was excellent. The doctor was very thorough, kind, friendly and approachable. I felt that everything was being done to investigate and improve my problem.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Helisa Bagheri
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I am extremely disappointed with the service at this GP practice. Over the years, both my children and I have been misdiagnosed multiple times, leading to serious consequences for our health. One particularly alarming experience involved a senior GP dismissing my concerns about perimenopausal symptoms. Despite expressing that I suspected I was entering perimenopause, she laughed and told me I was too young, completely disregarding that perimenopause can occur at various ages. She prescribed me the wrong medication, which worsened my symptoms to the point that I almost ended up in a mental health crisis.When I reported this to her, she casually offered antidepressants and didn’t even arrange a follow-up to check on my well-being. I had to take matters into my own hands and consult a private GP, who immediately confirmed I was perimenopausal and prescribed HRT. My symptoms improved almost instantly. This kind of negligence is unacceptable, and I have completely lost trust in this practice. I’ve even witnessed doctors Googling information in front of me, which makes me wonder—why bother going to the GP if I can just look things up myself? It seems they are only useful for minor issues like colds or flu. I would not recommend trusting them with anything beyond that.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Nuland
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Receptionists massive rude and unhelpful, it's like they go out their way to not help you. Very little care & compassion

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Hector Heath
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: In the short time I've been registered at the practice I've sent a few letters to my doctor to describe an ailment and the doctor has usually responded in 36 hrs or so. I handed one in on the 17/5/22 and when I hadn't heard anything by the 26th (today) I enquired why. Turns out the incompetent clowns lost it before the doc even saw it.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: James Gaskell
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Just had a receptionist constantly being condescending and passive aggressive when all I was asking was if I've had a tetanus shot in the last 10 years (asked to after advice from consultant from 111). I told her I wasn't happy with her behaviour and she told me to be quiet then put the phone down on me. I've had abuse off this receptionist before months ago. I suffer from multiple mental health problems including serve anxiety so speaking over the phone can be quite stressful. This was after waiting 15 mins on the phone already. Rang up again and another receptionist was polite and friendly, after the 1st experience and having problems before it's just not good enough.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: DAJ
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Brilliant health centre :-) Great reception staff, quick to respond and generally great to deal with - very lucky to have this in our area :-)

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Zoe Hague
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Fabulous GP, they have been brilliant with myself and my young family - always speedy to reply and very knowledgeable. Very lucky to have them as our Doctor's surgery.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Gaynor Swindlehurst
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I go for regular blood tests, ecg and blood pressure checks and to visit the doctor when i'm unwell

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Nicole “Future distant”
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: At first I was puzzled how a nhs institution could even have some bad reviews as it’s not a subway or a convenience store etc didn’t know that was a thing but after going here three times early morning missing work, the doctor kept texting on his phone ignoring multiple patients and promised to do definite ‘ biopsies’, in 2 weeks then when the time comes literally saying ‘nah let’s see what happens’ receptions really pleasant and helpful on the positive but the main doctor never seen anything like it in my life was shocking/genuinely unforgettable.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Lily Alex
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Handforth health centre have always been brilliant with me. I’ve sent in request via the online triage system and my doctor and other Handforth health workers have responded to message within 2 minutes! I feel well looked after and listened to when I have had face to face and phone call appointments too. There is never a wait and I can get through to them easily, appointments are available too. I have found the nurses and doctors to be lovely, and the receptionists to be very helpful and kind. I can’t fault this practice at all and highly recommend to anyone looking for a local practice.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Colin Mc (Canadaboygb)
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Hi Guys. had my left big toe analyzed and some preliminary work done before being booked an appointment at Congleton Memorial. I just want to say how pleased I was with the young lady who carried out the initial consultation and subsequent work on my toe,she was professional,considerate and very detailed in what she did(unfortunately cannot recall her name) .My toe has now recovered 99per cent thanks to her dedication. You've got a gooden there . Regards,Colin McMurray

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Sabina
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I went for a dermatology appointment at Handforth Health Centre. From the moment I entered the door, I found the personnel not very helpful. Then, I was taken by a very unpleasant nurse (of Asian origin, I think) to see my dermatologist. She was very moody and stayed with me during the appointment. I came with a mole I was worried about, so the dermatologist suggested checking all my other moles. However, I needed to take off my clothes in front of him without any separate curtains for privacy. The nurse was sitting on a chair next to the door in the meantime during all apointment. I felt really rushed taking my clothes off and throughout the entire appointment. Then, when the dermatologist finished the examination, I wanted to ask a few questions, but after my second question, the nurse opened the door to signal that the appointment was over and I had to leave. I have never experienced anything like that with the NHS or any medical organization anywhere in the world. It was an absolutely horrible experience.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: An excellent service every time, BUT... Access. The Handforth site car park is tiny (cosy!), with one disabled space. The surgery uses ACCURX to manage much of the admin processes including "ask for a consultation". The England wide NHS App doesn’t get much of a look in. We are pleased to have found this for our local GP.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Caitlin
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Helpful staff, made me feel at ease during my visit Friday 21st :)

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Eileen Clifford
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I have contacted this practice several times recently and as always I have received prompt attention from Dr Davies, Dr Halewood. Dr Nucomb and Dr Slater. I have always been treated with care, respect and dignity also with positive outcomes of their treatments . I would have no hesitation in recommending this practice. I have had an appointment with Dr Slater who was kind and considerate and very thorough in his examination. He then telephoned me 2 days later to ask how I was. Thank you to him and the other doctors and reception staff for their care.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: christine wilson

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I would like to leave a positive review for my GP practice following my recent appointment. She listened carefully to my concerns, explained things clearly, and made sure I understood the next steps regarding my care. Her calm and supportive approach made me feel comfortable throughout the consultation. I appreciate the professionalism and care I received from the practice.

You need to be professional and sort you manners out you horrible woman

Terrible service. A&E receptionists have better front of house and they are overworked and probably paid less! Ridiculous, will be moving to brookfield after that.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Catherine Sims

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Sonjia Clarkson
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: This surgery has been my life line. Especially Dr Nichols and Dr Whittaker. They have supported me through a very difficult time. They really do go the extra mile. I find the Reception team helpful too. Highly recommended

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Michael White
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Where to even begin. You call and the voice message tells you unless it is an emergency to use eConsult but economy only opens at 6pm and then you log onto eConsult and at 6.09pm a message pops saying the surgery is taking no more eConsult requests. You call to see a GP and you get triaged to a nurse or a paramedic or a musculoskeletal specialist. All of which to be fair are very good and often more useful than a GP. The practice pharmacist is also very helpful, Honestly though do any doctors even work here anymore?

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Racheal Shawcross
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: One stat is one too much Absolutely the worse surgery and communication! IN THE HISTORY IF THE NHS. You can never get on econsult. They make you feel thick, and that your troubling them. You hold for upto an hour to get through. You get fobbed off. You get given what ever appointment suits the doctors. Not one that is mutually convenient. Then you have to get back on the merry go round of being in the que for an hour. Receptionists well are very hit and miss. There is one particular receptionist (I won't name and shame) who is frankly god dam awful. Real chip on her shoulder and thinks she is some hierarchy in the GP world. To save your self the stress and grey hairs. DO NOT SIGN UP WITH THIS PRACTICE. I actually sat in the reception once. I was the only person in there. Two receptionist chatty chatting. I rang the telephone number and I was 7th in the queue. Neither of them where on the phone!!!!!!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Eric Quirk
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: When you (as an adult) really need urgent attention, Brookfield is excellent. Twice I have had real concerns as a result of a test or chest pains. Each time I was given the choice of a same day face to face or telephone appointment (after the 8am rush hour period). If you need more than 9 minutes interview it is readily available. Caring and thoughtful doctors and staff (including many on reception) despite the heavy pressure of increasing patient numbers. Also often answering queries on the phone.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Jay Camenzuli
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Ring the phone, no answer, walk in and all the receptionists are laughing and joking while my call is ringing. No one waiting, no queue, nothing. What the hell is going on!!!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Andrew Hine
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Very friendly and helpful but currently very difficult to get an appointment. recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Christine Forden

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Vicky

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Enid Smith
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Many thanks for excellent service given to to my Husband David Smith, by Dr Sumra recently, and also the reception staff

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: eric lane
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Had a great experience as I always do the lady who took my bloods was a breath of fresh air

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Asim Ali
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Attended with my mother, I have always found the Barrington medical centre to be helpful, we saw Dr Hussain, who was very kind and explained my mother’s problem well, a very competent young doctor.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: David Cowsill
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Very pleased with the efficient treatment and kind attention I received.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Shuaib akib
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: It was nice and lovely visit with family. We had an wonderful consultation with Dr. Hussain. We wish him all the best for his future.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Lindsay Roper
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I have visited Dr Hussain three times over the past three weeks He decided I needed to go to hospital on my first visit with low blood pressure and with the hospital help got me back on track with the two follow up visits and the referrals which are now all booked after finding blood in my urine he has been amazing and I am do grateful Dr Hussain had been great we have re visited my medication and made changes and he had Checked me out on both visits I am so grateful for all he has done plus the wider team at the surgery you are all amazing Thank you for all you have done for me Lindsay Roper

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Shikha Chauhan
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Dr Hussain was very attentive, patient and helpful in understanding the problem. He made sure I was comfortable and definitely that’s the kind of doctor visit that doesn’t make you anxious.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Bette Graves
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I had a lovely experience with Dr Hussain. He was very helpful and also very lovely to speak to. recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: R YU
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Dr Hussein was extremely kind and helpful, he was addressed all my concerns.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Gill Hogburn
